This study analysed 1,360 experimental class A GPCR structures to ask how captured G protein class information is represented in receptor coordinates, how far it transfers across receptor families, and how receptor-only coordinate models relate to the experimental specimens they derive from. Across 207 receptor–transducer units from 169 receptors, receptor sequence and endpoint geometry both predicted the captured class (Gs, Gi/o or Gq/11) under receptor-grouped validation, but transfer declined with evolutionary separation: geometry outperformed sequence at 50% sequence identity (macro ROC AUC 0.731 versus 0.638), and both were near chance at 30%. Among 34 receptors resolved with more than one transducer family, held-out receptor geometry retained a small captured-class signal that sequence cannot provide. By contrast, a compact four-feature receptor geometry recovered the annotated active/inactive state almost completely (ROC AUC 0.996), including when close homologues were separated. Functional coupling annotation showed that more than half of the mapped units come from receptors supported for at least two G protein families, and a specimen-level audit showed that most receptor-only coordinate models derive from transducer-containing cryo-EM specimens. Receptor coordinates in mature class A GPCR complexes therefore carry distributed, evolutionarily local information about the captured G protein class. A captured structural class should not be read as an intrinsic or exclusive coupling preference, and receptor-only coordinate models should not be equated with experimentally partner-free receptors
items.authors: Hossein Batebi

items.title: Bio-based furan- and bifuran-containing dilinoleic dimethacrylates: synthesis, photocuring, and network properties
items.authors: Amna Sadiq, Agata Goszczyńska, Miroslawa El Fray

items.title: Asymmetric selectivity at the glycoprotein hormone receptor allosteric site
items.abstract: Position 7.42 of the glycoprotein hormone receptors has been proposed as the determinant of mutual selectivity between LHCGR and FSHR, but has not been tested reciprocally. We compared the allosteric pockets of LHCGR with Org 43553 (PDB 7FIH) and FSHR with Cpd-21f (PDB 8I2G), and mapped each ligand into the other receptor by transmembrane superposition. Seven of 27 aligned contact positions diverge, a rate not distinguishable from the transmembrane background, and the mapping is markedly asymmetric. Cpd-21f placed in LHCGR makes a 2.31 Å contact with Tyr612, against 3.69 Å for the native His615 contact, and this is the single worst contact in the molecule. Org 43553 placed in FSHR meets no comparable barrier: 21 of 23 native contacts are preserved, burial increases, and the only sequence-driven loss is a hydroxyl-to-methyl van der Waals contact. Position 7.42 therefore excludes FSHR-selective ligands from LHCGR but does not explain why Org 43553 is weaker at FSHR. We further show that the morpholine tail of Org 43553 is buried rather than solvent-exposed and contacts only residues shared between the two receptors, accounting for published structure–activity data in which extensive variation of that tail failed to shift the LH:FSH ratio. A survey of ten orthologs identifies Phe515, the closest divergent contact and the only contact-shell position where LHCGR differs from a residue both paralogs share, as primate-specific; every non-primate examined, including all standard preclinical species, carries the paralog leucine. Finally, this pocket defeats several widely used scoring functions, which rank a reciprocal head-to-tail decoy above the crystallographic pose.
items.authors: Patrick Nasser

items.title: Oxidative strong metal-support interaction determines selectivity in supported Rh catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation
items.abstract: The restructuring of a catalyst’s interface with its support can be tailored via strong metal-support interactions (SMSI) in order to achieve desired product selectivity. SMSI is usually associated with reductive conditions, where a reduced oxide support covers a supported metal phase and alters catalytic activity. Here, pretreatment-dependent SMSI of rhodium nanoparticles supported on rutile titania is shown to control the selectivity profile for CO 2 hydrogenation reactions between methanation and the reverse water-gas shift reaction at 500 °C. Oxidative pretreatments at 400 °C were found to promote methanation with an initial rate of 5.1 mol/mol Rh /s for an O 2 pretreated sample and 5.8 mol/mol Rh /s for an O 2 followed by H 2 pretreated sample, whereas a H 2 pretreatment at 400 °C suppressed the methanation reaction to an initial rate of 0.25 mol/mol Rh /s. Instead of following classical methods of catalyst restructuring, such as sintering and reductive SMSI, the catalyst forms an SMSI overlayer under oxidative conditions, which restructures its active sites to selectively promote the methanation reaction. The effects of the restructuring are long-lived and dominated the catalyst selectivity even after more than 100 hours under reaction conditions. We demonstrate that this oxidative SMSI overlayer grows via a rhodium titanate intermediate and is necessary for creating active sites for methanation, shifting the catalyst’s selectivity away from the RWGS reaction. Theoretical calculations further demonstrate the thermodynamic favorability of TiO 2 overlayer growth under experimentally-relevant oxidative conditions. These results demonstrate that catalyst pretreatment conditions are a facile and effective tool for tuning the catalyst-support interface by allowing for the construction of an oxidative strong metal-support interaction that determines the product selectivity of supported rhodium catalysts.
items.authors: Jake Heinlein, Jake Erbez, Anastassiya Khan, Sabrina M. Gericke, Xiaobo Chen, Meng Li

items.title: Probing Nanoscale Carrier Dynamics in P3HT Blended with a Non-Fullerene Acceptor: Impact of Mixing on Device-Relevant Carrier Generation
items.abstract: High-performing organic photovoltaics (OPVs) rely not only on the appropriate energetics and interfaces for separating excitons into charges, but on distinct areas of donor-rich and acceptor-rich domains to transport those charges to electrodes once separated. In this work, we study a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) of well-studied poly(3-hexylthiophene-2,5-diyl) (P3HT) and a non-fullerene acceptor with an A1-D-A2-D-A1 motif, octyl rhodanine-thiophene-benzothiadiazole-thiophene-octyl rhodanine (ORTBT). Using device characterization and time-resolved spectroscopic techniques, we show that despite promising picosecond photophysical properties P3HT:ORTBT blends do not lead to long-lived charges due to overly-imbalanced mixing between the ORTBT acceptor and P3HT donor on length scales that are either too small or too large. We compare results with a prototypical BHJ, P3HT and PC61BM fullerene to understand the photophysical differences in the exciton dissociation dynamics. The significant mixing in P3HT:ORTBT disrupts the crystalline regions of the P3HT that are necessary for effective hole transport. This work demonstrates the need to consider both the chemical and physical properties of non-fullerene acceptors to achieve an optimal balance of donor-acceptor mixing that facilitates high exciton dissociation efficiency and long-lived carrier transport pathways in the bulk.
items.authors: Bryon W. Larson, Melissa K. Gish, Unsal Koldemir, David P. Ostrowski, Kathryn A. O’Hara, Sean E. Shaheen

items.title: LipidOracle: Ambiguity-aware lipid annotation across fragmentation methods
items.abstract: Tandem mass spectra (MS²) rarely determine a complete lipid structure, yet annotation software reports a best-scoring name and leaves users to judge whether the spectrum distinguishes it from other isomers. LipidOracle enumerates every isomer compatible with a precursor, converts the scores into probabilities with a softmax calibrated on standards, and reports the structural detail on which the credible candidates agree. An independent audit tests whether any observed fragment separates the reported structure from its closest rival. Annotation depth, from sum composition to double-bond position, is thus set by the evidence in each spectrum. The same inference handled collision-, electron- and ultraviolet photodissociation spectra, with only the fragment model exchanged. On standards, it located double bonds among thousands of candidate isomers with small credible sets, and in human plasma and mouse liver it named chains and double-bond positions only where the spectra supported them. The approach extends to any activation method whose fragments can be predicted.
items.authors: Vincen Wu, Abraham Moyal, Adriano Rutz, Nicola Zamboni

items.title: Majority-Rule of Enantiomeric Excess in Chiral Halide Perovskites for continuous tuning of chiroptical properties
items.abstract: Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = -100% to +100% corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%. By combining experimental spectroscopy with first-principles simulations, an approach we demonstrate to be transferable to tin-based analogues as well, we establish a quantitative structure-chiroptical property relationship across the full ee range. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra and absorption dissymmetry factors (gabs) exhibit a progressive, nonlinear evolution with increasing ee, consistent with cooperative majority-rule behavior governing chirality transfer from the organic cation to the inorganic framework. This effect is most pronounced in the 400-450 nm spectral region, where the CD signal tracks enantiomeric composition with high fidelity. Ab initio molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) quantitatively reproduces both the experimental CD spectra and gabs values across the entire compositional series, revealing that the macroscopic chiroptical response originates from the collective arrangement of chiral ligands, acting as a continuous dial for simultaneously modulating optical activity. This positions the ee as a general, accessible design parameter for chiroptical engineering across the family of halide perovskites.
items.authors: Mariagrazia Fortino, Hongki Kim, Amina Alehyane, Florent Barbault, Antonio Monari, Sascha Feldmann

items.title: Bulk Post-Polymerization Modification of a Single-Crystalline 2D Polymer via the Katritzky Reaction: A Modular Platform for Functional 2D Materials
items.abstract: Synthesizing two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) via single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) topochemical polymerization presents a dual challenge: preorganizing multifunctional monomers into two-dimensional crystal lattices and ensuring their polymerizable groups remain in close proximity to enable topochemical reaction in 2D. Consequently, topochemical 2DPs remain rare, and strategies for their post-polymerization modification, a standard tool in 1D polymer chemistry, are even more limited. Existing pyrylium-functionalized 2DPs suffer from severe steric hindrance caused by 2,6-di-tert-butyl substituents on pyrylium, restricting their post-synthetic Katritzky transformations solely to small nucleophiles like ammonia. To overcome this limitation, we synthesized a 2,6-di(isopropyl)styrylpyrylium triolefin monomer featuring 2,6-di-isopropyl substituents on pyrylium instead of 2,6di-tert-butyl. This subtle steric modification preserves topochemical polymerizability, while dramatically enhancing the reactivity of the resulting 2DP, enabling facile pore-wall functionalization with nucleophiles such as methylamine or ethylenediamine, to form Nmethyl- and N-(2-aminoethyl)pyridinium sites, respectively. Spectroscopic measurements show no detectable residual pyrylium in either derivative, while the ion-exchange capacity of the N-methyl derivative agrees with its theoretical capacity. These results establish solid-state pyrylium-to-pyridinium conversion as a strategy for post-polymerization modification of a topochemical 2DP precursor and represent a solid foundation for accessing a wide variety of topochemical 2DPs with engineered pore functionality.
items.authors: Valentin-Razvan Lupu, Antonia Neels, Paweł P. Ziemiański, Mirjana Dimitrievska, Vera Maria Kissling, Dorina M. Opris

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Nickel-Plated Steel Wool and Nickel Strip Electrodes for Hydrogen Production from Non-Potable Water Sources
items.abstract: Traditional water electrolysis imposes a significant freshwater demand. This study evaluates alternative non-potable feedstocks to reduce this dependency. We present a comparative performance analysis of user-fabricated, three-dimensional (3D) porous nickel-plated steel wool scaffolds versus conventional flat nickel control strips. Testing was conducted across tap water, rainwater, and greywater utilizing a near-neutral sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) electrolyte. Operational performance was quantified via volumetric hydrogen (H2) yield, Faradaic efficiency, and cost-normalized output (mL/$). The porous electrode significantly outperformed the flat strip, increasing Faradaic efficiency by 7% in tap water and 5% in rainwater. Furthermore, the 3D scaffold achieved up to an 8.7× greater hydrogen yield per dollar. These results demonstrate the bench-scale feasibility of low-cost, structured electrodes for reducing freshwater dependence in water electrolysis.
items.authors: Kyle Liou

items.title: Piezoelectricity-Induced Mechanical Bond Formation in Solid-state Using Mechanochemistry
items.abstract: Mechanochemistry, long promoted as a sustainable route to chemical synthesis, remains difficult to apply predictably to complex reactions due to a limited atomic-level understanding of how mechanical energy drives reactivity. Here, we demonstrated how piezoelectric polarization in tetragonal BaTiO3 directs solid-state mechanoredox chemistry, enabling electrode-free, reductant-free and solvent-free synthesis, for forming complex mechanically interlocked molecules for the first time. During ball milling, mechanically activated tetragonal BaTiO3 nanoparticles generate spatially separated redox sites that reduce viologen building blocks, promoting radical-pairing-driven pseudorotaxane formation and subsequent formation of stable [2] rotaxanes. First-principles calculations on BaTiO3 identify shear deformation as the dominant mechanical stimulus, where strain-induced polarization field produces an energetically favorable surface potential for the coupled redox reactions. These findings for the first time establish a direct mechanistic link between mechanical deformation, piezoelectric polarization, and mechanical bond formation, providing a predictive framework for sustainably constructing complex mechanically interlocked molecular architectures through piezoelectricity-mediated mechanochemistry.
items.authors: Surojit Bhunia, Pramita Kundu, Long Zhang, Sudipto Sinha, Partha J Das, Guangcheng Wu

items.title: Ultramild conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline mediated by metal organic alloy NiGraf in green solvent
items.abstract: The conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline can be carried out under ultramild conditions (35 °C under N2 at ambient pressure) with a 40% molar excess of hydrazine as reducing agent mediated by metal-organic alloy NiGraf in aqueous tetrahydrofuran, a green solvent. Conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline will optimally employ the stable and recyclable form of the NiGraf, consisting of reduced graphene oxide entrapped in jamborite nanoparticles, in renewable solvent system H2O/THF.
items.authors: Mario Orgnoni, Rosaria Ciriminna, Enrique Rodríguez-Castellón, Giuseppina Cerrato, Mario Pagliaro, Cristina Della Pina

items.title: Donor–Acceptor Integration Modulates Reverse Intersystem Crossing in Multi-Resonant TADF Emitters
items.abstract: Multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) compounds are attractive as emitters in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) owing to their high photoluminescence quantum yields and narrowband emission. However, these emitters generally have moderate reverse intersystem crossing rate constants (kRISC), which causes triplet exciton accumulation and leads to, amongst other excitonic processes, triplet-triplet annihilation. This process results in significant efficiency roll-off in OLEDs at high luminance. Here, we report the photophysical properties of a 2 boron–nitrogen doped MR-TADF emitter, tCzBN, and two of its derivatives, SpAc-tCzBN and TRZ-SpAc-DBN, using time-resolved absorption and emission spectroscopy. Kinetic modelling of their photophysical behavior reveals that combining a donor–acceptor core with the MR-TADF moiety in TRZ-SpAc-DBN results in a higher kRISC than tCzBN and its donor-appended analog, SpAc-tCzBN, while preserving the narrowband emission of the MR-TADF unit. We attribute this enhancement to the lower effective adiabatic singlet–triplet energy gap (∆EST) and stronger spinorbit coupling in this molecular design.
items.authors: Pratiksha Dad, Kittimeth Thammanatpong, Mahni Fatahi, Peter M W Gill, Eli Zysman-Colman, Girish Lakhwani

items.title: Parameter Recovery and Noise Sensitivity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Michaelis–Menten Kinetics: A Benchmark Against Classical Nonlinear Least Squares
items.abstract: This study evaluates a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating Michaelis–Menten kinetic parameters from sparse and noisy concentration–time observations. The investigated system follows the ordinary differential equation , with a true maximum reaction rate of , Michaelis constant , initial substrate concentration , and a simulation duration of 10 time units. Synthetic observations were generated using numerical integration and additive Gaussian noise at 1% and 5% levels. The PINN consisted of a fully connected neural network with three hidden layers, 32 hidden units, and hyperbolic tangent activation functions. Its trainable kinetic parameters were constrained to positive values using the softplus transformation. Training minimized a weighted combination of data error, initial-condition error, and differential-equation residual error. To address optimization instability, the study used an increased training budget of up to 8000 epochs, early stopping, multiple initialization seeds, and cross-validation for selecting the physics-loss weight. A classical nonlinear least-squares estimator was used as a comparison method. In a diagnostic example, the corrected PINN produced errors of 1.04% for and 5.10% for , compared with 2.99% and 19.32% for the classical method. However, across the small benchmark of 18 replicates, the classical method generally achieved lower median errors and lower prediction RMSE, especially under 5% noise. The results show that the PINN can recover kinetic parameters accurately in favorable conditions, but its performance remains sensitive to data quantity, noise, optimization, and experimental design.
items.authors: Mateen Ur Rehman

items.title: Analysis of fine-tuned foundation interatomic potentials and their knowledge distillation into a cluster expansion for Ni–Pt ordering thermodynamics
items.abstract: Predicting alloy ordering thermodynamics requires the energies of thousands of atomic arrangements at fixed composition, far more than density functional theory (DFT) can routinely provide. Fine-tuned foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are a promising alternative, but whether they resolve the small energy differences between arrangements has not been established. Here, we examine this for fcc Ni–Pt in three steps. First, six foundation MLIPs fine-tuned on the same DFT data are evaluated on a 64-structure DFT benchmark. All six reach low global errors (2-20 meV/atom), but these errors are dominated by a composition-dependent offset that cancels between arrangements of one composition. We therefore evaluate the configurational energy Econf, the energy of a structure relative to the other structures of the same composition. After relaxation only four models reproduce DFT Econf (R2conf = 0.93-0.94), whereas fine-tuned eqV2 and CHGNet do not (0.48 and 0.37). Second, we locate the source of this failure. Linear probes on the frozen embeddings of all six models recover EconfDFT (R2 = 0.87 to 0.98), showing that the learned representations are intact. The accuracy is lost during relaxation: through the cell response of eqV2 and through inaccurate forces near the energy minimum in CHGNet. Third, we use the most accurate model, fine-tuned eqV3, as a teacher for knowledge distillation into a cluster expansion. Trained on 6,434 MLIP energies instead of 64 DFT energies, the distilled cluster expansion reduces the held-out DFT error from 4.43 to 2.79 meV/atom and reproduces the DFT-based transition temperatures within 167 K, comparable to the 120 K statistical uncertainty of the DFT-trained expansion itself. These results establish when fine-tuned foundation MLIPs can be trusted for alloy ordering and provide a route for transferring their accuracy to thermodynamic simulations.
items.authors: Jungjae Hwang, Jaejun Lee, Channyung Lee, Elif Ertekin, Kyoungmin Min

items.title: An Algorithm for computing Three- and Four-Body Density Matrices from CASCI Wavefunction and AI-Assisted Code Optimization
items.abstract: Three- and four-body reduced density matrices in the active space are required for second-order n-electron valence perturbation theory (NEVPT2) following complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) calculations. We developed an algorithm to generate these computationally demanding quantities by extending the pi-CASCI program, which is based on the graphical symmetric group approach (GSGA). A manually written prototype was subsequently optimized through AI-assisted code optimization, resulting in substantially improved performance.
items.authors: Kiyoshi Tanaka, Takahiro Katagiri, Tatsuya Nakano, Yuji Mochizuki

items.title: Where the vibronic coupling lies: promoting-mode frequencies and second-order rate theory for reverse intersystem crossing in multiresonance TADF emitters
items.abstract: Rate models for reverse intersystem crossing in multiresonance delayed-fluorescence emitters usually place the vibrational spectrum on one promoting mode near 75 meV and treat the triplet–triplet vibronic coupling at second order. Neither approximation has been tested at scale. This work computes nonadiabatic couplings and signed spin–orbit vectors (PBE0/def2-SVP, Tamm–Dancoff) for all 121 emitters of the Hagai et al. compilation, and full vibrational spectra for 17 of them. The coupling-weighted promoting quantum has a median of 173 meV, in the aromatic ring-stretch region, with about 25 modes carrying 90% of the squared coupling. Collapsing the spectrum onto a 75 meV oscillator inflates the coupling by a factor of 1.5, and second-order theory then fails: over 120 emitters its rate departs from exact diagonalisation of the vibronic problem by a median of 0.49 orders of magnitude and lies further from experiment. At the computed 173 meV the median departure is 0.10 orders, although 21 emitters still differ by more than an order. On a multimode model that preserves the residual coupling matrix it falls to 0.02 orders for the 17 emitters with spectra, against 0.61 and 0.23 orders for the single-mode model on the same molecules. Both multimode treatments overestimate the measured rate for 15 of the 17 emitters, by a median of 1.2 orders, so the remaining error lies in inputs they share. For these emitters the breakdown of second-order theory comes from the single-mode reduction; the near-resonant regime remains to be tested with full spectra.
items.authors: Ramarao Tata

items.title: ProtMutMap: Predicting Protein Binding Free Energy Changes Using Multiple-Mutation Networks
items.abstract: Predicting changes in binding free energy ΔΔ G caused by multiple mutations at protein−protein interfaces requires accounting for nonadditive interactions between mutations, which an additive approximation based on single mutations cannot capture, and for the dependence on the computational pathway in stepwise approaches that introduce mutations sequentially. Here, we propose ProtMutMap, a method that integrates information from multiple pathways in a network whose nodes represent target variants and variants containing subsets of their mutations, and whose edges represent free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations for residue substitutions. ProtMutMap simultaneously estimates the binding ΔΔ G of each variant from all edge values using Huber loss. We compared ProtMutMap with the additive approximation and the stepwise method at 30 evaluation points, including intermediate variants, using a multiple-mutation dataset comprising 7 protein complex systems derived from SKEMPI2. ProtMutMap achieved a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 1.13 kcal/mol, lower than that of either comparison method. ProtMutMap also yielded lower prediction errors than Rosetta flex ddG. These comparisons with experimental values demonstrate that integrating multiple pathways through variants containing subsets of the target mutations improves binding ΔΔ G predictions for protein variants with multiple mutations.
items.authors: Kairi Furui, Masahito Ohue

items.title: Biomimetic remodelling of lipid membranes using DNA nanostructures
items.abstract: The remodelling of biological membranes underpins a diverse range of sophisticated cellular processes, from cell crawling to mitosis to pathogen infection cycles. A refined understanding of the biophysical principles governing lipid bilayer remodelling is necessary to engineer ever-more advanced behaviours in microrobots, like synthetic cells, with disruptive applications in both fundamental biology and advanced biotechnology. Owing to its ability to afford control over structural and functional properties at the nano-scale, DNA nanotechnology has emerged as a prime toolkit to engineer, program, and host biomimetic responses within lipid bilayer membranes. This Perspective review surveys advances on biomimetic membrane remodelling pathways coordinated by DNA nanostructures. I discuss strategies to prescribe the interactions of DNA nanostructures with lipid bilayers, and summarise progress to drive membrane remodelling events including lateral patterning, out-of-plane restructuring, fusion, and scission. Finally, I discuss current challenges alongside the yet untapped potential of nucleic acid nanostructures in membrane bioengineering to coordinate sophisticated behaviours in synthetic cells.
items.authors: Roger Rubio Sánchez

items.title: Less is more in mixture modeling: every molecular vector is a map, yet the mixture is the territory
items.abstract: Predicting mixture properties is a key challenge across domains, yet current deep-learning designs approach it blindly: they largely reuse the single-molecule recipe, compressing each molecule into a vector and predicting the mixture’s property from these vectors. We find that mixtures, as components multiply, depend increasingly on precise topological information. We therefore advocate a new design: model the mixture directly as a unified atomic system with complete and precise molecular topology. A simple instantiation of this design reaches or approaches the best published baselines across diverse domains, and indicates that the failures of existing vector-based models on some tasks stem from the same thing: every molecular vector is a map, yet the mixture is the territory.
items.authors: Xiao Yang, Guanghao Song, Zihan Xu, Yanan Yang, Baojiang He, Lingbo Ji

items.title: Localized Sequential Backflow Ansatz for Scalable Neural Quantum States
items.abstract: Neural Quantum State Architectures have been shown to have high accuracy on a variety of molecular and lattice systems, often outperforming traditional methods. This work replaces the all-to-all paradigm of current neural quantum states with a localized recurrent sequential backflow mechanism. Results have empirically exhibited approximately quadratic wall-clock scaling over the system sizes tested, namely the hydrogen chain with atom with length of H 10 to H 400 , suggesting a viable path towards a scalable Neural Quantum State.
items.authors: Dylan Liu-Walter

items.title: IRexp: A database of experimental infrared band lists from open literature
items.abstract: IRexp is a collection of experimental infrared band lists (cm⁻¹ peak positions) mined from open chemistry literature, with author-reported ¹H/¹³C NMR strings and resolved structures where available. The research corpus holds 121,233 records from the PMC Open Access Subset and the Chemotion repository, including 57,646 structure-linked entries and 39,118 IR + ¹H + ¹³C + structure quadruples. The public dataset of record contains 88,519 CC-BY/CC0 records released under CC-BY-4.0, with ShareAlike and non-commercial records distributed separately under their source licences. Every record carries a source identifier and a per-record licence stamp. Technical validation covers automated transcription, recall-proxy, and consistency audits. IRexp targets multimodal training, retrieval, and structure-elucidation tools that need structured, attributable experimental peak lists.
items.authors: Ilkham Yabbarov, Rudra Sondhi, Rodrigo A. Vargas-Hernández

items.title: Hyperfine dynamics as an internal control of reactive-oxygen-species output in a triplet-born flavin–superoxide radical pair
items.abstract: When reduced flavin is activated by molecular oxygen it forms a spin-correlated radical pair—a flavin semiquinone and superoxide (O₂•⁻)—born in the triplet manifold, because ground-state O₂ is a triplet. Its singlet/triplet recombination gates the branching of reactive oxygen species, and the pair is realised in the electron-transfer flavoprotein, whose output is field-dependent. Radical-pair theory almost always treats the hyperfine tensor as fixed and the field as the variable. We invert that: with the field held fixed, what upper bound does a time-dependent active-site hyperfine coupling place on the singlet yield? We pose a coefficient inverse problem with the principal-axis components Aₖ,ₐ(t) as the control and solve it for the genuine triplet-born flavin pair (two ¹⁴N at I = 1, three protons; dimension 288) at a 200 ns lifetime. A time-dependent coupling raises the yield to ΦS = 0.290 at 50 µT, against 0.241 for the best constant coupling in the same admissible set (1.20×) and 0.203 for the molecule’s own couplings (1.43×); the reduced models give larger gains, so they overestimate the effect. The optimum places 76% of its modulation in the first 0.5 µs and is smooth and numerically near-singular, unlike the bang–bang optimum of the external-field problem. These are coherent yields obtained over a control set far larger than conformational motion can access—an upper bound on an upper bound—with spin relaxation, the dipolar coupling and the superoxide g-anisotropy left unmodelled. The falsifiable quantity is the dynamic-over-static gain, not the absolute yield.
items.authors: Pablo R. Castello, Pablo Jiménez, Carlos F. Martino

items.title: Redox-Paired Activation of Sulfur Hexafluoride Enables Nucleophilic C(sp3)–F Bond Formation
items.abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is a potent greenhouse gas whose direct use as a fluorine source in organic synthesis remains underdeveloped. Here, we disclose complementary photoredox and electrochemical strategies for nucleophilic fluorinations with SF6, merging oxidative formation of carbocation intermediated from alkoxamines, carboxylic acids, or thiols with SF6 reduction, the latter providing fluoride for C(sp3)–F bond formation. The photochemical protocol efficiently converts electronrich substrates and tolerates a broad range of functional groups, whereas paired electrolysis extends the reaction to electronically deactivated substrates. Together, the two methods enable fluorination of diverse benzylic and aliphatic substrates, including late-stage fluorination of structurally complex derivatives of pharmaceuticals, natural products, and agrochemicals.
items.authors: Aniruddha Biswas, Demetra Zambardino, Tanja Gulder

items.title: CuBr-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Decahydroquinoxaline-Based Bis(propargylamines): Application to the Synthesis of an Axially Chiral Allene
items.abstract: A CuBr-catalyzed one-pot protocol provides access to decahydroquinoxaline-based bis(propargylamines) from readily available terminal alkynes, aromatic aldehydes, and a C2symmetric chiral diamine. The three-component coupling proceeds at 120 °C within 12 h, affording the products in 58–93% yields with diastereomeric ratios of up to 99:1. The synthetic utility of the protocol is illustrated by the ZnI2-mediated conversion of a representative bis(propargylamine) (7a) into the corresponding axially chiral allene (8a) with 90% ee. This approach enables the stereoselective construction of bis(propargylamines) and demonstrates their application as precursors to axially chiral allenes.
items.authors: Laxman Alakonda, Mariappan Periasamy

items.title: Insights into Electrolyte Effects on Interfacial Kinetics and Transport in Porous Redox Flow Battery Electrodes: A Multiparadigm Modelling Study
items.abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their decoupled energy and power densities. Electrolyte formulation plays a key role in determining the electrochemical performance of RFBs, influencing interfacial kinetics and transport within porous electrodes. Herein, we develop a multiscale modelling framework to investigate the coupled effects of the electrolyte concentration (Methyl Viologen (MV) and NaCl) and the fibrous 3D microstructure on the porous transport and electrochemical kinetics in organic RFBs using a kinetic Monte Carlo model. We link this interfacial kinetics to the advection-diffusion transport in stochastically generated carbon felt electrode microstructures through Lattice Boltzmann Method simulations via an interpolation-based coupling. We use two performance descriptors, the fibre-averaged rate of potential loss and convective area fraction, to quantify the kinetics and transport effects, along with their interplay. While increasing MV concentration enhances the interfacial kinetics, it limits the transport within the electrode microstructure. The interfacial kinetics shows to be nontrivially governed by the supporting electrolyte. A surface area-permeability trade-off appears across microstructures with different electrolyte concentrations. This multiparadigm modelling workflow provides mechanistic insights between porous transport and interfacial electrochemical kinetics, enabling the coupled optimization of microstructures and electrolytes in RFBs.
items.authors: Avaneesh Balasubramanian, Francisco Fernandez, Alejandro A. Franco

items.title: Multigram Copper-Catalyzed Azidodeboronation of Alkenyl Boronates
items.abstract: A multigram synthetic approach to alkenyl azides based on copper-catalyzed azidodeboronation of alkenyl pinacol boronates was described. The optimized protocol relied on the use of Cu(OAc) 2 as the reaction promoter, which provided higher, reproducible yields and did not cause uncontrolled decomposition of the reaction mixture, unlike the CuSO 4 ·5H 2 O-based protocol reported previously. The method was applicable to β-, β,β-, and α,β-substituted substrates, including those bearing electron-withdrawing groups and saturated O -, N -, and S -heterocyclic motifs. Some alkenyl azides were prepared on up to 21 g scale, and their thermal behavior was evaluated by thermogravimetric analysis. The synthetic utility of the products was demonstrated through the preparation of a substituted pyrrole and 1-alkenyl-1,2,3-triazoles. Furthermore, a one-pot azidation – click reaction protocol enabled the direct conversion of alkenyl boronates into the corresponding triazoles without isolation of unstable or highly volatile alkenyl azide intermediates, thereby broadening the accessible substrate scope.
items.authors: Maksym Kovalenko, Yevhen M. Ivon, Yaroslava Kovalchuk, Kristina Bakhmatska, Dmytrii Kryvenchuk, Yaroslav Yakivets

items.title: Enhanced Catalysis via Multiscale Force Propagation in All-Enzyme Glucose Oxidase Hydrogels
items.abstract: Enzyme-based biomaterials are sustainable catalytic platforms with applications in biosensing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and environmental remediation. A key challenge is developing universal immobilisation strategies that preserve activity without requiring enzyme-specific optimisation. One promising approach is the photochemical cross-linking of native tyrosine residues to form self-supporting all-enzyme hydrogels, where the enzyme serves as both the catalytic and structural component. However, rational design of these materials requires understanding how gelation-induced forces propagate through the network and influence enzyme function. Here, we combine experiments and simulations to establish a multiscale framework linking hydrogel assembly, force propagation, and catalysis in glucose oxidase hydrogels. By varying the lamp intensity used during photochemical cross-linking, we control gelation kinetics and examine their consequences across molecular and network length scales. Slower gelation reduces enzyme unfolding and produces more loosely packed hydrogel networks with enhanced dynamic correlations and increased free volume around enzyme active sites. Integrating experimental measurements with modelling reveals that these structural changes enhance catalytic performance through altered force transmission across the network. Our findings demonstrate that enzyme activity is regulated not only by local active-site processes but also by collective mechanical interactions spanning multiple length scales, establishing network mechanics as a new design principle for functional biocatalytic materials.
items.authors: Harrison Laurent, Matt D. G. Hughes, Zoey Mikol, Ahmad Boroumand, Dimitra Katrantzi, Najet Mahmoudi

items.title: Two barriers to benchmarking structure-based virtual screening against the AcrB efflux pump: a sample-size ceiling and an identifiability failure
items.abstract: Background. The AcrAB-TolC system is the principal constitutive efflux pump of Escherichia coli and an attractive adjuvant target. Virtual screening campaigns against its distal binding pocket have been published without the retrospective validation standard elsewhere in the field. This study asked whether such a benchmark can be built from the published literature. Methods. Compounds reported as AcrB inhibitors were filtered against an independent reproducibility screen and assigned to a binding site by the strongest structural or mutational evidence available. Property-matched decoys, a library-representative background and a class of reported-but-non-reproducing inhibitors served as negatives. A pilot docking screen against the hydrophobic trap of 5ENQ was re-analysed under the curated labels, with areas under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve reported with analytic and bootstrap confidence intervals. Two controls were pre-specified: a wrong-site control, and a ligand-only ablation deleting the receptor entirely. Results. Of 49 compounds reported as AcrB inhibitors, 38 have been independently retested and 17 reproduced; 13 maps to the distal pocket and 5 have a co-crystal there. Two barriers follow. With 5 actives the 95% interval cannot be narrower than ±0.26; reaching a conventional ±0.06 would require 94 actives, while raising the decoy ratio from 40:1 to 500:1 narrows the interval by 0.8%. More seriously, the ligand-only ablation reached 1.000 against a docking area of 0.707: deleting the receptor improved performance. 4 of the 5 co-crystal actives are analogues spanning 2 scaffolds, with a median pairwise ECFP4 similarity of 0.574 against 0.077 to the negatives; every active–active pair lies above the decoy-exclusion threshold of 0.35 and every active–negative pair below it. Conclusions. A retrospective docking benchmark for the AcrB distal pocket cannot currently be built. The first barrier is quantitative and yields to more confirmed inhibitors of any kind; the second is qualitative and yields only to inhibitors that are chemically unlike one another. Screening against this pocket therefore proceeds unvalidated and cannot be validated until structurally diverse confirmed inhibitors exist, which is a medicinal-chemistry result rather than a computational one. The curated compound table, the metrics implementation with its unit tests and the analysis notebook are released.
items.authors: Ibrahim Ibrahim Shuaibu

items.title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystalline Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
items.abstract: Molecular transport in supramolecular crystals under nanoscale confinement may exhibit different regimes across widely separated timescales, making their experimental characterization particularly challenging. Here, oxygen quenching of aromatic luminophores incorporated into a β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane crystalline matrix in aqueous suspensions is investigated using steadystate and time-resolved luminescence spectroscopy. The probes provide emission lifetimes ranging from tens of nanoseconds to approximately 15 s. Effective bimolecular quenching rate constants referenced to the concentration of dissolved oxygen in the surrounding aqueous phase decrease from approximately 10 9 to 5×10 4 L mol -1 s -1 across the probe series. The decreasing branch approximately follows a power-law dependence on the unquenched emission lifetime, k q ∝ τ 0 -0.8 , whereas probes with lifetimes longer than approximately 10 ms exhibit a nearly constant quenching rate. A diffusion–reaction model relates the measured constants to temporal averages of the oxygen encounter flux and accounts for the finite excitation duration. Under the assumptions of comparable probe accessibility and diffusion-controlled quenching, the observed scaling is consistent with subdiffusive transport with an effective anomalous exponent of approximately 0.4. A finite range of local transition rates within a quenched random-barrier model provides a possible explanation for the crossover to the long-time plateau. These results show that lifetime-dependent luminescence quenching provides a means of probing oxygen transport over widely separated timescales and testing transport models in nanoscale-confined molecular systems.
items.authors: Denis E. Makhrov, Irina V. Ionova, Alexander A. Korlyukov, Alexander D. Volodin, Georgy A. Yurasik, Mikhail V. Alfimov

items.title: Design Rules for Mixed Rutile PGM Oxides
items.abstract: Oxide solid solutions have important industrial applications including catal-ysis that require high stability under operating conditions. The stability of solid solutions is usually predicted using structural similarity, with low lattice mismatch resulting in stable solid solutions and high lattice mismatch resulting in unstable solid solutions. While this works for most solid solutions, some such as yttria-stabilised zirconia break the rules and remain stable due to other factors. Here we use density functional theory to study the substitutional solid solutions of the rutile platinum group metal (PGM) oxides IrO 2 and RuO 2 . These PGM oxides are commonly used as oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts in proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysers and both suffer from degradation in the harsh acidic conditions. In an effort to stabilise the PGM oxides and determine what factors affect the mixing thermodynamics, we mix the PGM oxides with each other and four other rutile oxides with different properties. Our results for the nine unique systems, including both PGM-only and PGM/non-PGM solid solutions, show that the mixing thermodynamics can be predicted using two new mixing rules. Firstly, rutile oxide solid solutions have negative mixing enthalpies when both solutes are metallic and positive mixing enthalpies otherwise. This is independent of all other factors. Secondly, increasing the electronegativity difference between solute metals decreases the mixing enthalpies as long as the first rule remains unbroken. This was shown by NbO 2 having the most favourable mixing with the PGM oxides despite its larger lattice. We hope these new mixing rules can be used to design new stable solid solutions of rutile oxides such as IrO 2 and RuO 2 .
items.authors: Alp Eren Samli, Rachel Nathaniel Kerber, Laure Briquet, Misbah Sarwar, David O. Scanlon

items.title: Pore-Engineering Enhances Low-Temperature Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conduction in Two-Dimensional Polymer Lithium Ion-Battery Electrodes
items.abstract: Understanding the fundamental relationships between ionic and electronic charge transport in polymer systems is essential for the systematic development of bioelectronic, optoelectronic, and energy-storage devices that leverage these materials. A classic strategy to improve ionic conductivity in mixed conducting materials involves attaching ionophilic oligoethylene glycol (OEG) groups to charge-carrying polymers. However, installation of oxygen heteroatoms into the framework of mixed ionic-electronic conductors also induces unintended structural changes in both the native and operational states, thereby adding complexity to structure-property relationships. Two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) are crystalline, planar macromolecules with well-defined one-dimensional channels that can be functionalized without significantly disrupting the crystalline scaffold. We designed topologically equivalent 2DPs with either ionophobic or ionophilic pore structures and studied these materials as lithium-ion battery cathodes. We observed that OEG pore-functionalized 2DP electrodes exhibit higher redox potentials, lower charge-transfer resistances, and higher overall achievable capacities than ionophobic-functionalized 2DP electrodes. Additionally, we found that pore-functionalized 2DP electrodes have higher capacity retention at Arctic temperatures (-30 °C) than commercially available inorganic cathode materials. Our findings demonstrate that pore functionalization is a viable strategy for enhancing the performance of 2DP mixed ionic-electronic conductors and engineering them for extreme environment deployment.
items.authors: Ani N. Davis, Eva Vásquez-Barillas, Kiana A. Treaster, A M Mahmudul Hasan, John D. Langhout, Diana Graham

items.title: Models building models for discovery of graphene metamaterial design principles in the context of failure
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence assists scientific discovery, but most agents operate previously developed instruments. Whether an agent can build an instrument, translating physical theory into reliable measurements and testable predictions, then use it for open-ended research remains open. Here, from a single prompt, an AI agent built and validated an atomistic simulator and conducted 96 simulations across ten graphene architecture families. At matched mass, load paths governed strength, and tilted slits revealed distinct failure mechanisms. Human–AI collaboration examined larger strains and hierarchical architectures. Sliding slit edges exhibited sequential geometric reconnection; hierarchical veins redistributed load, compartmentalized damage and deflected cracks. Selected larger hierarchical designs were about 25% stronger, with at least one-third greater work to failure, than equal-mass, equal-size controls. These results demonstrate a workflow where AI agents build scientific models and use reflective reasoning to falsify, validate and refine physical understanding, while human–AI collaboration drives mechanistic discovery and engineering of complex materials.
items.authors: Markus J. Buehler

items.title: Compositional flexibility and structure dynamics of Strätlingite
items.abstract: Strätlingite, Ca 2 Al(AlSi)O 2 (OH) 10 ·2.25H 2 O a phyllosilicate found in nature and in ancient Roman concrete, was investigated for its synthesis conditions, phase stability, and thermal and chemical degradation mechanisms. Contrary to previous reports, phase formation was observed to be complete after ~3 days of setting, using hand-ground precursors, while the applied water:solid ratio has only minimal effect on purity of the resulting strätlingite. The chemical stability field is rather narrow, and off-stoichiometry in the initial Ca:Si:Al ratio of the starting materials promotes the formation of poorly crystalline C-(A-)S-H side phases, which are difficult to detect by XRPD and may compromise complementary data interpretation. Thermogravimetry, variable humidity in situ XRPD and water sorption measurements reveal a reversible hydration below 100 °C, that is reflected in gradual changes of the lattice parameters and unit cell volume up to 2%. Above 100 °C irreversible changes to the crystal structure occur, resulting in the loss of the long-range order, which is complete at 200 °C and further. Strätlingite remains chemically stable during setting LC 3 cement formulations, making it a potential cement additive, provided the temperatures remain below 100 °C.
items.authors: Artem Shevchenko, Keshia Morell, Rotraut Merkle, Fabian Heck, Igor Moudrakovski, Bettina V. Lotsch

items.title: ADMET-Informed Machine Learning Prioritization of Hydrogel-Associated Compounds for Nanocarrier Evaluation
items.abstract: Experimental screening of large hydrogel-associated chemical collections is slow and resource-intensive. We developed an ADMET-informed machine-learning workflow for 2060 HydrogelDB-linked compounds, using the median of a separately reported admetSAR3.0 biodegradability-related output to define higher- and lower-score classes and the remaining 115 predicted ADMET properties as model inputs; preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, probability calibration, and threshold selection were confined to the training partitions of nested cross-validation. The calibrated linear SVM achieved a mean held-out MCC of 0.9116 ± 0.0222, an F2-score of 0.9662 ± 0.0112, and a ROC–AUC of 0.9904 ± 0.0048; performance remained high after proxy-feature removal and feature-family ablation, whereas structure-focused models showed a weaker but detectable signal. Strict eligibility criteria retained 19 candidates. Six-component ranking under changes in model outputs and weights identified D-Alanyl-D-Alanine, Prolyl-Glutamate, and Pro-Asp as the most stable leading candidates. N-Glycylalanine showed lower ranking stability, with Isoleucylglycine as the main alternative. All shortlisted compounds require experimental validation of biodegradability, hydrogel formation, and nanocarrier performance.
items.authors: Zeinab Hosseinyazdi, Seyed Majid Hashemianzadeh

items.title: Heavy Metal-Binding Peptide Phytochelatin Drives Membraneless Compartmentalization and Biomineral-Like Structures via Nanoparticle Formation within Condensates
items.abstract: Phytochelatin is a heavy metal-binding biogenic peptide found across different organisms that helps cells mitigate cytotoxicity by chelating metal ions. Yeasts produce phytochelatin to chelate intracellular cadmium and sequester it as cadmium metal sulfide nanoparticles. These nanoparticles were proposed to be stored within cytoplasmic microcompartments, although it remains unclear whether they are stored within membrane-bound or membraneless compartments. Here, we focused on the structure of phytochelatin and hypothesized that it can form membraneless compartments with positively charged biomolecules, which are capable of internal cadmium sulfide sequestration. Indeed, mixing phytochelatin with natural polysaccharide chitosan led to the instant formation of membraneless condensates. Moreover, Cd and S were preferentially accumulated within the condensates relative to other elements and CdS nanoparticles formed inside them. These nanoparticles exhibited crystalline features, with sizes of 2–3 nm and structures comparable to those of the CdS particles observed in cells, which predominantly correspond to the hawleyite structure. This study demonstrated that heavy metal-binding peptides can participate in the formation of membraneless compartments and internal sequestration of nanoparticles. Our findings further indicate a potential role of phytochelatin-based membraneless compartments in spatially controlled intracellular biomineralization and heavy metal sequestration for cellular detoxification, which remains to be explored in vivo.
items.authors: Yeseul Park, Péter Pekker, Isabelle Ly, Morgane Pasco, T-Y Dora Tang, Mihály Pósfai

items.title: In situ Activation of Ni(II) with Boronic Acids and Application of a Phosphasilinane Ligand enable the Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling of Deactivated (Hetero)Aryl Chlorides
items.abstract: The important substitution of costly palladium catalysts with earth-abundant nickel alternatives in Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions is still problematic for challenging substrates, such as heteroaryls and (hetero)aryl chlorides. In this context, we report the application of low Vbur and electron-rich biaryl-based phosphasilinane ligands in nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction of electron-rich (hetero)aryl-chlorides with aryl boronic acid substrates, at catalyst loadings as low as 0.5 mol-% on gram-scale synthesis. To overcome the use of unstable Ni(0)-sources, the activation of cheap and bench-stable L2NiCl2 precatalysts with boronic acids was investigated and successfully applied, e.g., in the synthesis of intermediates for agrochemical and pharmaceutical products. Furthermore, this method enabled the synthesis of bench- and base-stable L2Ni(3-furyl)Cl complex, which was directly applied in cross-coupling reactions.
items.authors: Christoph Kremser, Dino Berthold, Alexander F. Siegle, Oliver Trapp

items.title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
items.abstract: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations. However, constructing these reduced models requires numerous user-defined decisions, including selection of the starting structure, identification of atoms to include in the QM region, and definition of truncation strategies for QM-only models, all of which can substantially influence the resulting calculations. QMzyme aims to provide the community with a flexible and extensible framework for automated, systematic generation of QM-based enzyme models, enabling researchers to more rigorously evaluate how model construction decisions influence computational outcomes while improving reproducibility and transparency across workflows. By facilitating high-throughput generation and analysis of QM enzyme models, QMzyme supports largescale, data-driven investigations of enzyme structure, function, and reactivity. This effort is especially crucial for the creation of large, chemically consistent datasets that can support emergent artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for accelerated digital discovery in enzymology and biocatalysis.
items.authors: Arkanil Roy, Young Woo Kim, Heidi Klem

items.title: On the enzymatic synthesis of ketone-containing oligomers and their processing into sustainable crosslinked materials
items.abstract: In this work, two ketone-containing pre-polyesters based on dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (pDMOG) and dimethyl 1,3-acetonedicarboxylate (pDADC), were obtained via a solventless polymerization reaction in presence of Lipase B from Candida antarctica as the biocatalyst. 1 H-NMR indicated diol conversions over 90% for both monomers, while GPC analysis revealed differences between the two systems, with pDMOG reaching a M n of ≈ 8 kDa ( M w ≈ 30kDa) while pDADC reached a M n of ≈1.5 kDa ( M w ≈ 2.5 kDa). Molecular docking studies were performed to investigate the productive accommodation of the substrates and corresponding oligomeric products within the CaLB active site. Priamine TM 1071 (PR) was then used to crosslink these polymers using a solvent-free and catalyst-free reaction, showing that the network formation was directly governed by the molecular structure of the ketone-containing pre-polyester precursor. The thermal stability of the obtained materials showed an improvement at higher temperatures when compared with the neat pre-polyesters. DSC analyses showed that pDMOG and pDADC are semicrystalline materials, while the crosslinked materials led to fully amorphous systems. The rheological behaviour was also analysed, confirming that the crosslinked materials have temperature-dependent viscoelastic properties. These results can provide new perspectives for the design of processable crosslinked polymer systems obtained from bio-derived precursors by using chemo-enzymatic methods.
items.authors: Diana-Ionela Dăescu, Nathan Jourdainne, Christian Vigo, Giacomo Damonte, Anamaria Todea, Orietta Monticelli

items.title: Direct Asymmetric Hydroalkoxylation of Styrenes Through Flavin Brønsted Acid Biocatalysis
items.abstract: Direct addition of free alcohols across alkenes would provide a concise route to chiral ethers, but controlling alkene activation, nucleophile capture, and stereochemistry remains difficult. We evolved an oleate hydratase, an enzyme that naturally adds water across alkenes, to favor alcohol addition instead. The resulting enzyme catalyzes intermolecular hydroalkoxylation of electron-rich styrenes in aqueous solution, reaching up to 80% yield and 99% enantiomeric excess. Evolution reshaped an alcohol-binding pocket around a conserved flavin-centered core, allowing alcohol to compete with water. Mechanistic studies support a redox-neutral cycle in which protein-bound neutral FADH 2 acts as a Brønsted acid to protonate the alkene. By placing direct asymmetric hydroalkoxylation within an engineerable enzyme scaffold, this work opens a route to expand both alkene and nucleophile scope through protein engineering.
items.authors: Shubhanshu Jain, Raúl Lago-Saavedra, Jill McLachlan, Axel Jeibmann, Matúš Gajdoš, Silvia Dehne

items.title: Evolutionary Design for Anion-Derived Interphase Stability
items.abstract: High-concentration electrolytes (HCEs) improve lithium-ion battery cycling by shifting interphase formation from the solvent to the anion, producing a more stable inorganic-rich interphase at the anode. However, the anions for HCEs has been mainly studied on FSI− and TFSI−, and the anion itself has received little systematic exploration relative to the solvent and the salt concentration. Here, anion chemical space is searched using evolutionary framework that couples genetic algorithm with quantum-chemical descriptors of reducibility, solvent coordination, and charge delocalization. Substructure analysis of the evolved populations identifies a sulfinimide (N−=S) core as the recurring motif in place of the sulfonyl chemistry of the reference anions, and a combinatorial scaffold-branch library built from these motifs exhibits distinction between the electronic and intermolecular contributions to anion performance. Charge localization is governed by the scaffold while solvent binding is set neither by scaffold nor by branch alone but by their specific pairing and by whether the two arms are chemically distinct. Higher-level solvation show that the leading candidates from the selected anion set exceed both baseline anions in bulk solvation, and transport calculations exhibit that every candidate carries a smaller Li+ first shell and diffuses faster than both baselines at concentrated salt content. Replacing a single sulfonyl oxygen with an imide nitrogen reorganizes the anion around a delocalized, asymmetrically substituted core and opens a salt chemistry for HCEs distinct from the sulfonyl imides in use today.
items.authors: Esra Ulgey Akgun, Brett M. Savoie

items.title: A numerically verified analytical framework for immobilised-enzyme packed-bed reactor design in the kinetically controlled regime applied to dihydroxyacetone production
items.abstract: Continuous-flow biocatalysis can decouple enzymatic productivity from the cellular growth constraints inherent to fermentation, but exploiting this advantage requires a reactor design framework that links enzyme kinetics, immobilisation penalties, and catalyst deactivation to industrially relevant performance metrics. We develop an analytical quasi-steady-state (QSS) plug-flow reactor model for immobilised-enzyme packed-bed reactors (PBRs) operating under first-order catalyst deactivation, and verify its transport assumptions against a two-dimensional axisymmetric COMSOL™ finiteelement model. The close agreement between the analytical and numerical solutions confirms that reactor performance is kinetically controlled across the investigated operating window, and yields a closed-form expression for the time-averaged space–time yield (𝑆𝑇𝑌 ) that factorises into five independently controllable design levers. We apply this framework to a feasibility study on the continuous enzymatic conversion of formaldehyde to dihydroxyacetone (dha) using immobilised formolase (FLS), a reaction of interest for C1 biomanufacturing. Parametric mapping across substrate concentration, enzyme loading, and immobilisation-induced activity penalties, combined with sensitivity analysis incorporating enzyme deactivation, identifies substrate concentration, enzyme loading, substrate affinity (𝐾M), and catalyst stability as the principal parameters governing productivity, and shows that continuous immobilised FLS operation can sustain greater than 8-fold higher timeaveraged productivity than fermentation across the full range of product yields and operating scenarios considered. Beyond the specific case study, the verified QSS framework and its design-lever decomposition are directly transferable to other immobilised-enzyme PBR systems, offering a general route from laboratory kinetic data to quantitative reactor and catalyst design targets for continuous biomanufacturing.
items.authors: P. E. Roy, W. Rostain, F. Brossard, C. Smith, J. Molloy, L. Fruk

items.title: Project ⟨χ|χ⟩: Extending Dragonball towards Quantum Vibrational Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Semiclassical dynamics is able to add nuclear quantum effects to classical trajectories, in an approximate yet effective manner. However, moving from classical to semiclassical dynamics requires the careful consideration and implementation of many tools, especially in the case of ab initio semiclassical dynamics. In this paper, we present Project ⟨χ|χ⟩, a set of tools designed to extend the capability of the recently released Dragonball beyond quasi-classical trajectories. First, we improve Dragonball accessibility by providing a set of PySCF scripts to substitute ab initio software. Second, we expand Dragonball infrastructure by adding Adiabatic Switching and Hessian Database to make it semiclassical-ready, and CandyBeam to safely store the data. Finally, we showcase these tools by computing the semiclassical spectra of H2, H2O, CO2 and H2 ·C60 using Frieza, a code to compute Gaussian Wavepacket autocorrelation spectra, fully compatible with Dragonball.
items.authors: Giacomo Botti, Antonino Famulari, Sophya Garashchuk, Giacomo Mandelli

items.title: Nucleotide-mediated catalytic peptide synthesis from aminonitriles
items.abstract: Aminonitriles are accessible from simple feedstock compounds and their hydrolysis offers an abiotic route to life’s amino acids on the early earth. However, controlled aqueous polymerisation of amino acids into peptides remains challenging. Here we show that peptides can be directly generated and elongated by aminonitriles when the latter are coupled to nucleotides as a phosphoramidate. Upon thiol catalysis and pH shifts, a series of selective reactivities drives iterative peptide bond formation in water. The high energy nitrile bond of aminonitriles circumvents amino acids’ need for concurrent activation chemistry in peptide elongation. Coupling the building blocks of life’s central biopolymers in this manner provides a pathway for early integration of peptides into biology.
items.authors: Luis Ohlendorf, Jyoti Singh, Erica Park, Sofija Spric, Qian Zhang, Josh Maiklem

items.title: Structure-Based Prioritization and Electronic Tuning of Cinnamate-Bearing Natural Products at Falcipain-2 and Falcipain-3
items.abstract: Electronic descriptors can prioritize substituents on model electrophiles, but whether those choices persist in intact natural products across receptor states remains uncertain. We tested cinnamate-bearing natural products at falcipain-2 (FP-2) and falcipain-3 (FP-3). Screening 1,012 South African Natural Compounds Database records yielded 185 motif-bearing parents, 174 with paired profiles. Receptor-normalized Glide XP ranking placed acteoside and aloeresin C alone on the dual-target Pareto front; six composites agreed at Spearman ρ ≥ 0.93. A protocol-matched FP-2 benchmark showed limited but statistically resolvable enrichment (ROC-AUC 0.548, 95% CI 0.505–0.590; 0.641, 0.586–0.698 for covalent actives). In a para-substituted methyl-cinnamate series, OH→NO₂ increased global electrophilicity from 2.22 to 3.69 eV while decreasing the β-carbon Fukui response from 0.166 to 0.026 as 61% of the added-electron response shifted to the nitro fragment; fragment-level trends persisted across ESP and Mulliken partitions, whereas atom-condensed indices did not. In the intact glycoside, para-chlorination improved the FP-3 Docking Score by 0.77 units (more negative) at pH 7.0 but redistributed the cinnamoyl core across the pose ensemble (median displacement, 8.7 Å) without conventional halogen-bond geometry, so the score gain did not reflect simple pose conservation. Moving one proton within the FP-2 catalytic dyad shifted the matched-pair contrast by 3.89 units and altered one-third of the library by more than the substituent effect; at pH 5.5, the FP-3 contrast reversed to +0.62. Thus, substituent effects that survive score-selection and sampling checks can remain conditional on protonation-state treatment, placing ligand tuning and receptor-state uncertainty on the same quantitative scale.
items.authors: Olaniyi Victor Olaniru, Clement Odunayo Ajiboye

items.title: Evaluation of alternative polymerases for biocatalytic synthesis of modified oligonucleotides
items.abstract: Enzymatic synthesis of modified nucleic acids is gaining a lot of traction. Most approaches involve the combination of modified nucleoside triphosphates and engineered polymerases capable of accepting such altered substrates. Such enzymes are obtained through engineering campaigns based on directed evolution, positional saturation mutagenesis, and rational design approaches potentially guided by in silico methods. However, most polymerase evolution/design approaches rely on a restricted diversity of enzyme chassis. Here, we have performed a biochemical characterization of two polymerases, the human DNA HsPolθ and the heterodimeric archaeal DNA primase PriSL from Pyrococcus abyssi, capable of synthesizing oligonucleotides under both template-dependent and -independent reaction conditions. We have assessed their capacity at accepting nucleotides with modifications at any position of the scaffold as well as reversible terminators. We have also evaluated the possibility of using high salt conditions to force polymerases to incorporate single nucleotides. Overall, our study reveals that both polymerases are tolerant to modifications and could be amenable to engineering campaigns to identify variants capable of producing hypermodified XNAs for de novo nucleic acid synthesis approaches.
items.authors: Fabienne Levi-Acobas, Germain Niogret, Sophie Battédou, Gilles Gasser, Markel Martinez Carranza, Marc Delarue

items.title: Thermal pathway reconstruction exposes a reliability gap for AI-guided materials design
items.abstract: AI-guided materials design increasingly connects candidate generation with processing and experimental planning, yet recognizing a material’s final thermal endpoint is not the same as reconstructing how it gets there. We benchmarked closed-book reconstruction of source-qualified differential scanning calorimetry event maps for 30 molecular materials using GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5. In the primary API experiment, models recovered terminal melting in 194/216 opportunities (89.8%) but other thermal transitions and pathways in only 105/318 (33.0%). Additional frontier-model configurations reproduced this endpoint-pathway gap. Providing source-reported preparation and scan conditions did not improve pathway reconstruction: recall changed by −6.5 percentage points (95% CI, −14.5 to +0.9) for Sol and −4.9 points (−13.6 to +4.5) for Opus. Frontier models can therefore recognize where a material’s thermal trajectory ends while failing to reconstruct the state changes determining how it gets there.
items.authors: Olga Lavinda

items.title: Reductive insertion of a trivalent metal leading to the isolation of Prussian blue-type EuIIIFe3[Fe(CN)6]3
items.abstract: Reductive insertion reactions selectively modify three-dimensionally bonded solid-state structures through the addition of an elemental metal by electronation of the host structure and insertion of the metal cation into the host cavities for charge balance. However, with rare exceptions, this class of reactions has been largely restricted to insertions of monovalent metals. The reductive insertion of divalent and trivalent metal ions is intrinsically limited by their very slow diffusion through a host lattice at low temperatures and instability of a host lattice in the presence of these metals at high temperatures. These limitations originate from strong coordination of multivalent guest species to anions within the host lattice. By using coordinatively saturated anions such as cyanide in Prussian blue analogues, only relatively weak coordination modes to guest cations are available within the host structures, suggesting these host structures may participate in multivalent metalations. Herein, we report reductive insertion of europium into Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ] under relatively mild conditions by reaction with EuI 2 at 150 °C in N-methyl-2-pyrolidone. The formation of the half-ferrous product, Eu III Fe 3 [Fe(CN) 6 ] 3 , is an exceptionally rare reductive insertion of a trivalent metal, and the first example of a phase pure Prussian blue (A n+ 1/n Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]; A = metal cation) isolated with either a lanthanide or multivalent A-site metal. The resulting compound exhibits a distribution of iron oxidation and spin states not observed in previously reported Prussian blue phases of the form M I Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]. The valence of Eu 3+ was confirmed by a combination of X-ray absorption, 57 Fe Mössbauer, and magnetic susceptibility measurements, which informed a possible reaction mechanism invoking redox exchange between the ferrous host, Eu 3+ guest ions, and excess Eu 2+ in solution.
items.authors: Shain S. Mollick, Sayantani Sur, Jacob W. Fritsky, Nilarun Koley, Ryan S. Storteboom, Jason F. Khoury

items.title: Low-Cost, Home Synthesis of Vaterite: A Factorial Study of Calcium Source, Temperature, Citric Acid Modification, and Mixing Intensity
items.abstract: This paper presents a low cost, home-accessible method for synthesizing vaterite-type calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) using consumer-available materials and simple household tools. Vaterite is a metastable CaCO₃ polymorph of interest for biomedical, filler, and coating applications, but existing synthesis protocols typically require laboratory-grade reagents and equipment, limiting accessibility for independent researchers. The two required precursors, sodium carbonate (from baking soda) and calcium acetate (from eggshells and vinegar), were prepared in house. A 16-factor design then tested how calcium source, solution temperature, citric acid addition, and mixing intensity affect morphology. Optical microscopy (400×) of the first successfully produced sample (condition 3-D: cooled calcium chloride, citric acid added, strongly mixed) showed small, circular clusters with a flour-like texture consistent with vaterite morphology. Qualitative comparison of the remaining conditions suggests that citric acid addition is associated with finer textures more than mixing intensity, though this remains unconfirmed under magnification for most samples. This is presented as an interim record of an ongoing study. Crystallographic confirmation (XRD/FTIR) and microscopy of the remaining samples are planned as direct follow-up work. The primary contribution at this stage is a documented, reproducible, low-cost synthesis protocol together with one positive proof-of-concept result.
items.authors: Omar Alaa El-Din El-Jeheny

items.title: Optimal sparging and mixing for enhanced mass transfer in U-loop bioreactors across scales
items.abstract: Scaling up the utilization of CO 2 for fuel and protein production requires designing large-scale reactors that can enhance gas-liquid mass transfer rates. Here, the gas sparging and phase mixing strategies are optimized in the case of a 608 m 3 U-loop reactor using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The optimization is made possible by constructing a surrogate model that maps the design variables to the quantity of interest that captures the mass transferred per unit of energy expended. It is found that the optimal design consists of distributing as many spargers as possible. A separate analysis investigates how optimization can be conducted across scales, operating conditions and model assumptions. It is shown that optimal designs are primarily affected by the reactor scale if the reactor volume ratio between the industrial scale and the lab-scale is greater than 100.
items.authors: Malik Hassanaly, Pranav Jain, Mohammad J Rahimi, Federico Municchi, Devon Sigler, Hariswaran Sitaraman

items.title: All-Optical Spin Coherence in a Photosynthetic Electron-Transfer Metalloprotein
items.abstract: Optically addressable, biocompatible spin qubits represent promising platforms for quantum sensing. However, current efforts have focused on genetic encodability and microwave-based approaches thus far limited to organic radicals. Utilizing time-resolved Faraday rotation, we measured electron spin coherence in plastocyanin, a protein in the photosynthetic electron transport chain. Persisting hundreds of picoseconds, this is the first measurement of spin coherence in a metalloprotein under ambient conditions. We show how the protein’s active-site geometric and electronic structure responsible for biological function also enabled a spin–photon interface. A related blue copper protein—azurin—also demonstrated all-optical spin coherence. The ability to measure bioinorganic spin coherence under functional conditions foreshadows metalloproteins as native quantum sensors and opens questions about the potential role of spin coherences in electron transfer.
items.authors: Christian A. Totoiu, Erica Sutcliffe, Demetrios A. Dresios, Ryan G. Hadt

items.title: Scoring close linker analogues in PROTAC ternary complexes: A matched-pose study of VHL-recruiting SHP2 degraders
items.abstract: Linker optimisation in targeted protein degradation remains largely empirical, and a computational method able to rank close analogues before synthesis would be valuable. Whether current methods can do so has not been tested against the smallest chemical difference that changes potency. Here two VHL-recruiting SHP2 degraders that differ by exactly one methylene, P9 and P10, were compared across 27 ternary complex arrangements generated for both compounds, so that in every comparison the protein–protein geometry was held fixed and only the degrader varied. RxDock interaction scores did not distinguish them (p = 0.66). Prime MM-GBSA favored P9 by 8.1 kcal mol−1, agreeing in direction with the reported potency order (p = 0.040), but the preference was overturned by removing any of twelve individual poses and arose entirely from the generalized-Born solvation term; the nonpolar contribution was zero (−0.01 kcal mol−1, p = 0.97). Interface geometry computed from coordinates alone was indistinguishable between the two ensembles, with buried surface areas differing by 0.23%, and the computed energies were uncorrelated with interface size across a 2.9-fold range (r2 ≤ 0.10). Two further observations emerged: rigid-body docking score did not predict ternary competence, since none of the highest-scoring 1% of arrangements accommodated either degrader, and the longer linker reached ten more arrangements while closing no better within those both could bridge. End-point scoring of single minimized ternary complexes therefore does not resolve a one-methylene linker difference, even when it recovers the correct direction, and conformational averaging rather than a different energy function is the most likely route to improvement. The ternary complex models reported here are the first for this series.
items.authors: Tasniqul Islam

items.title: DrugForge-ADMET v0.3.0: An auditable BRICS-based workflow
items.abstract: Early hit discovery normally begins with a physical or virtual collection of small molecules. Public resources such as PubChem, ChEMBL and ZINC have broadened access to chemical space, but using them effectively still requires retrieval, standardization, filtering, deduplication, three-dimensional preparation and provenance management; many laboratories also lack an in-house screening collection. We present DrugForge-ADMET v0.3.0, an open-source RDKit workflow intended to provide a compact, auditable starting set when a prepared library is unavailable. The software decomposes 30 inspectable, sp3-enriched seed templates into BRICS fragments, recombines them, sanitizes the products, and applies deterministic physicochemical rules, structural-alert catalogues and explicitly labelled descriptor-based risk proxies. Seed/reference similarity is assessed with radius-2, 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints and Tanimoto similarity; score-first diversity selection limits redundancy. Selected structures are exported as CSV and as SDF records with ETKDGv3 conformers followed, where parameterized, by MMFF or UFF optimization. In three fixed-seed technical validation runs, each capped at 10,000 enumerated products, 61, 157 and 194 candidates were selected. Across 412 outputs, 411 canonical SMILES were unique, all 412 SDF records were readable and all contained three-dimensional conformers. The pooled median values were molecular weight 355.50, cLogP 1.55, TPSA 79.25 Å2, fraction sp3 0.706, three rotatable bonds, one aromatic ring and QED 0.845.
