Reliable identification and quantitation of the alkaloid class require chromatographic resolution in addition to mass spectrometric detection. Here, we present a validated QuEChERS extraction protocol and LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous determination of ten kratom alkaloids in 42 commercially available pressed tablets. The method was linear from 0.05 to 2.0 μg/mL (mean R2 0.992), with limits of detection ranging from 0.0005-0.044 μg/mL, recoveries of 80-120% for seven of ten analytes, and interday precision below 12.5% for nine of ten analytes. MGM-15 was detected in 31 tablets (73.8%) at a median concentration of 6.62 mg/g. Twenty-two of 26 quantitative label claims were not met; in three products, the claimed alkaloids were nearly absent despite total alkaloid content exceeding the stated claim by more than sevenfold. Two products marketed without kratom claims contained eight and nine of the ten target alkaloids, respectively. Combining MGM-15 detection with the 7-OH:MIT ratio identified 34 of 42 products (81%) as semi-synthetically modified. These findings emphasize the need for reliable, robust, and label-independent analytical surveillance of this evolving product class.
items.authors: Ana Barovic, Mitchell L. Ellinwood, Shelby Blanchart, Alexandra E. McDevitt, Giovanni A. Ramirez, Joseph Hamilton

items.title: A Novel Mononuclear Nickel Complex as a Precatalyst for Ionomer-Dependent Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity
items.abstract: In electrocatalytic water splitting, ionomer-catalyst interactions can significantly influence electrochemical performance. Molecular metal–organic complexes offer a tractable platform to investigate such interactions. Here we report a novel nickel–2methylimidazole complex, [Ni(2-MeIm)4(NO3)]NO3, with Ni@N4O2 coordination environment. The structure of this new material is established by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and supported by vibrational spectroscopy and thermal analysis. We evaluate the complex as an oxygen evolution reaction precatalyst in 1.0mol L−1 KOH and show that its apparent activity depends strongly on the ionomer used in the catalyst ink. With Aemion+, an anion-exchange ionomer the catalyst reaches 10mAcm−2 current density at an overpotential of 0.331V, whereas the same catalyst formulated with Nafion exhibits a markedly reduced activity with an overpotential of 0.403V. The impedance spectra recorded at 1.6V vs RHE show considerable differences in charge-transfer resistances between the two formulations, consistent with differences in interfacial charge-transfer kinetics. We propose that specific catalyst–ionomer interactions may modulate active-site accessibility and the in situ transformation of the molecular precursor into catalytically competent NiOOH.
items.authors: Neethu Kochukunnel Varghese, Serena De Negri, Pavlo Solokha, Antonio Comite

items.title: Scientific World Models: Toward Closed-Loop Scientific Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from task-specific scientific tools toward foundation models, generative design, research agents, and autonomous laboratories. Despite this progress, most systems remain organized around isolated predictions or local workflows. They rarely maintain an evolving account of scientific objects, predict the consequences of interventions, or learn systematically from computational and experimental evidence. This article introduces scientific world models as a core paradigm for closed-loop scientific intelligence. A scientific world model reconstructs the physical state of a scientific object and its corresponding epistemic state—what is known, uncertain, or contested—from partial, multimodal, and instrument-mediated observations. It models action-conditioned state transitions, explores plausible futures under scientific constraints, and supports the selection of measurements, simulations, experiments, and process interventions according to scientific value, information gain, cost, feasibility, and risk. The new evidence then updates the state, hypotheses, and subsequent actions. On this basis, we propose a three-layer architecture of scientific perception, cognition, and action. Perception turns the physical world into traceable scientific observations and state representations. Cognition combines data-driven models with scientific laws, mechanistic knowledge, and simulation to interpret current states and reason about possible futures. Action connects model reasoning to computation, instruments, experiments, and physical processes. We further distinguish the scientific world model core from foundation models, scientific agents, digital twins, and autonomous laboratories, and outline domain instantiations, maturity levels, evaluation criteria, and open technical challenges. This framework provides a common basis for developing scientific AI systems that can observe, reason, act, and improve through evidence.
items.authors: Huan Wang, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong

items.title: Substituent Effects Govern the Fidelity of Responsive Persulfide Donors
items.abstract: Persulfides (RSSH) are important intermediates in sulfur transfer and trafficking in redox biology, yet the intrinsic chemistry of these molecules complicates the design of small molecule donors that deliver persulfides on demand. Here, we investigate how specific parameters of both the persulfide payload and disulfide structure in selfimmolative donors influence persulfide release, H2S formation, and the susceptibility to degradation by biological thiols. Notably, we demonstrate that many common structures used for persulfide delivery likely do not produce the intended payloads due to a combination of unexpected thiol-disulfide exchange reactions prior to donor activation or subsequent instability of the released persulfide. Using a family of esterase-activated donor constructs, we show that geminal dimethyl substitution at the benzylic position accelerates self-immolative payload release and decreases unwanted thiol-disulfide exchange prior to donor activation. We also establish that steric protection of the release persulfide strongly influences its downstream fate, with unhindered cysteinederived persulfides generating substantially more H2S than sterically protected penicillamine-derived systems. Importantly, thiol exchange studies reveal that insufficiently protected caged disulfides can be consumed rapidly by GSH before trigger activation, thereby diminishing donor integrity. Together, these results establish that the functionality of persulfide donors is governed by steric protection, which influences the competing pathways of donor activation, thiol exchange, persulfide persistence, and H2S formation. More broadly, this work establishes design principles for high-fidelity persulfide delivery and provides a framework for interpreting biological studies in which persulfide donors may participate in competing sulfur transfer and sulfur release pathways.
items.authors: Ismail Ismail, Michael D. Pluth

items.title: From prediction to process control: a critical review of machine learning in reactive dyeing of cotton
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive exhaust dyeing of cotton uses large amounts of water, salt, alkali and heat, partly because the recipe and programme are fixed when a batch starts. This review asks whether learned models, acting on the machine during a batch, have been shown to reduce that consumption. An OpenAlex search (2003 to September 2026, 862 records) and web searching identified 27 primary studies of learned, rule-based, model-based or search-based methods, or inline monitoring, in reactive dyeing of cotton. Each was coded by setting and by how far its output reached the process. Twenty-two stop at offline prediction, three only measure the bath, one advises an operator and one acts automatically; 24 are laboratory studies. No included study documents a learned model automatically changing an outcome-level decision (dye, salt or alkali quantity or timing, temperature programme, or rinse endpoint) during a batch. The one automatic controller, a fixed rule timing alkali injection at pilot scale, is not learned. A check on 135 studies of all fibres agreed. Reported fixation spans 40 to 70%, and no study has measured how much of the shortfall control could recover. Two priorities follow: measuring that share, and a matched-batch trial of learned, rule-based and operator control.
items.authors: Sk. Mainuddin, Tinon Turja Majumder, Md Shajjad Khan Faisal

items.title: Detection of Molecular Oxidation States in Dye Sensitized Solar Cells-Relevant Organic Dyes Eosin Y Through Optical UV/Vis Absorption Spectrum Changes
items.abstract: This study investigates oxidative degradation mechanisms of the non-metallic organic dye Eosin Y in order to examine precisely how they influence the light-harvesting efficiency (LHE) of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs). Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) computations with ABINIT are used to construct the molecular geometry and electronic configuration of the dye in its neutral form, oxidized adduct state , and oxidized state with excited electron. From the basic Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) to its Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO) energy gaps and Ultraviolet-Visible (UV/Vis) absorbance spectra obtained from the computations, it is evident that both photo-oxidation and oxygen addition render the molecule inactive, resulting in up to 90% reduction in extinction coefficient and near disappearance of the visible absorption spectrum. In summary, this project provides a molecular-level interpretation of the efficiency reduction experienced in organic DSSCs due to oxidative degradation.
items.authors: Alibek Kadralinov

items.title: Mean First-Passage-Time-Directed Bias Optimization with Gaussian-Kernel Markov Models
items.abstract: Rare transitions limit the direct simulation of molecular kinetics and complicate the design of enhanced-sampling biases that accelerate specific events without obscuring their mechanism. We develop a data-driven framework in which biased trajectory data are combined using dynamic histogram analysis and represented by either conventional grids or normalized kernel-anchor memberships to construct finite row-stochastic kinetic models. These models are used to adapt a bounded bias by directly minimizing an absorbing mean first-passage time (MFPT) objective, while reactive-current diagnostics independently assess whether accelerated trajectories preserve the reference transition mechanism. We first test the kernel-induced representation in equilibrium free-energy reconstruction and then apply the kinetic optimization framework to progressively more challenging rareevent problems, including membrane permeation, multidimensional barrier crossing, and a metastable molecular rearrangement. The benchmark calculations show that MFPT-directed biasing can efficiently promote target arrival and that soft kernel states provide a flexible alternative to rigid spatial discretization. At the same time, pathway analysis shows that faster arrival does not imply preservation of the underlying transition mechanism. A confounded high-dimensional stress test further exposes the limitations of projected kinetic models when the relevant dynamical coordinates are unresolved.
items.authors: Qingying Wang, Tingyue Zhou, Baowen Li, Christian Jorgensen, Edina Rosta

items.title: RealBind: a leakage-controlled benchmark for experimental PXRD and Raman structure retrieval
items.abstract: We present RealBind, a benchmark for retrieving crystal structures from experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and Raman spectra. It contains 3,288 curated candidate structures, of which 1,468 have linked measured PXRD patterns, and 16,005 experimental Raman spectra, of which 10,547 are linked to structures. We provide quality-control records, prototype-held-out and composition-held-out splits, and evaluation protocols that state candidate-library size and the chemical information available at retrieval time. On a 492-candidate prototype-held-out library, a contrastive model trained on simulated PXRD reaches 78.5% Recall@10 on simulated queries but 5.3% on measured queries; physics-inspired corruption raises measured-query Recall@10 to 34.4%. A model-free correlation against simulated candidate patterns, with no preprocessing beyond the common Q-grid resampling and the measuredwindow mask, achieves 82.8% Recall@10 on the same test library. In a separate split comparison, 44% of random-split test structures have a structure-matched training counterpart; measured-query Recall@10 is 59.1% on that split versus 20.7% on the prototype-held-out split, although test populations and libraries also differ. Holding the trained model and 420 queries fixed, restricting the candidate library and pre-screening candidates by the ground-truth element set of the query’s structure, used as an oracle chemistry-conditioned diagnostic, raises Recall@10 from 27.1% to 99.1%; 37.6% of filtered queries have a single candidate. A Raman-to-structure baseline reaches 34.7% Recall@10 on heldout mineral spectra against 979 candidates in the pooled evaluation and 45.7% on the 485-candidate test-only library, which includes no validation structures. RealBind provides an experimental test bed for comparing learned methods with simple simulation-based matching under explicit, leakage-aware protocols.
items.authors: Preyansh Srivastava

items.title: Bridging Azahelicene Enables Circularly Polarized Luminescence in a Dinuclear Ytterbium(III) Single-Molecule Magnet
items.abstract: Modern coordination chemistry employs increasingly sophisticated building blocks to design compounds and molecule-based materials with unusual combinations of properties relevant to emerging technologies. A notable example is the incorporation of helicenes as chiral ligands in luminescent and magnetic lanthanide complexes, which can give rise to circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) or magneto-chiral dichroism (MChD). Lanthanides are particularly wellsuited for CPL owing to their intraconfigurational 4 f -4 f transitions with long excited-state lifetimes and sharp, well-defined emission bands. Herein we present a new low-coordinate Yb III dinuclear complex [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenolate; azahelicene = benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]benzo[4,5]imidazo[2,1-k][1,10]phenanthroline), where the two Yb III luminophores are bridged by the optically pure azahelicene ligand as the source of chirality. Additionally, the reported compound is a single-molecule magnet (SMM) thanks to the synthetic strategy that enables control of the coordination sphere around the Yb III ion. The combined experimental and theoretical magneto-optical studies conducted for both enantiomers of [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] reveal a direct link between the crystal structure, the related crystalfield splitting, and the observed magnetic and chiroptical properties. First of all, the introduction of the azahelicene into the coordination sphere of the achiral luminescent Yb(BHT) 3 parent compound was achieved with the retention of its SMM behavior. Most importantly, however, its incorporation as an integral component of the molecule enabled the observation of circularly polarized near-infrared (NIR) emission from Yb III . Three CPL bands were detected in the NIR, including the most intense signal at 978 nm with the luminescence dissymmetry factor glum = |0.035|, as well as a rare CPL emission above 1050 nm.
items.authors: Gabriela Handzlik, Salauat R. Kiraev, Mathieu Gascoin, Maxime Grasser, Stephan Guy, Bruno Baguenard

items.title: Comprehensive Quantum Chemical Interaction Analysis of Whole Protein–Ligand Structures in BindingDB Using the Fragment Molecular Orbital Method
items.abstract: Understanding protein–ligand interactions based on their electronic states is important for elucidating molecular recognition and supporting structure-based drug discovery. In this study, we performed fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations, a quantum chemical approach, for a comprehensive set of experimentally determined protein–ligand complexes derived from BindingDB. Ligand–amino acid residue interactions were quantitatively characterized using inter-fragment interaction energies (IFIEs) and pair interaction energy decomposition analysis (PIEDA), and were compared with molecular mechanics (MM) interaction energies. The comparison revealed residue- and interaction-dependent differences between the FMO and MM descriptions, with particularly distinct behavior for interactions involving aromatic residues. Comprehensive IFIE/PIEDA analysis further revealed characteristic energetic contributions associated with amino acid residue type and ligand charge, including dispersion contributions involving aromatic residues and charge-transfer contributions associated with hydrogen-bonding interactions. A case study of MAPK14 demonstrated that the resulting dataset can identify residue regions commonly involved in ligand recognition and distinguish residue-level interaction patterns among individual ligands. These results provide a systematic quantum chemical perspective on diverse protein–ligand interactions and establish a quantum chemical resource for complementing structural, experimental, and conventional MM-based analyses.
items.authors: Shuhei Miyakawa, Naoko Konami, Ruri Mihata, Rikuto Osaki, Ayaka Masuda, Tomoka Taguchi

items.title: Screening Protein Conformational Responses by Molecular Friction Sensing
items.abstract: Small-molecule drugs often act by stabilizing specific protein conformations, yet most biophysical screening platforms report binding affinity or kinetics without directly capturing structural response. Here we introduce molecular friction sensing (MFS), a screening-compatible approach that detects ligand-induced changes in protein conformation through changes in hydrodynamic drag exerted on electrically switchable DNA origami nanolevers. Across a diverse protein panel and under physiological conditions, the method quantitatively reports protein size and resolves ligand-dependent conformational shifts with sub-Angström sensitivity. In maltodextrin-binding protein, cognate and non-cognate maltodextrins produced distinct friction signatures that mirrored their biological roles. In a carbonic anhydrase screen, molecular friction sensing identified compound-dependent conformational responses among SPR-validated binders, revealing that affinity and kinetics do not predict structural outcome. Molecular friction sensing therefore adds a structural dimension to interaction analysis and provides a route to prioritize drug candidates by the conformations they induce.
items.authors: Pablo Porragas Paseiro, Lukas Aufinger, Alfred Kick, Tereza Jahodová, Veronica Hamer, Ulrich Rant

items.title: Precision of Gaussian, Lorentzian, and pseudo-Voigt peak fitting under Gaussian noise
items.abstract: Discriminating subtle differences in measured signals is essential to scientific discovery. Knowledge of the attainable precision limits of fitted peak parameters and the physical and statistical factors that determine them provides a rational basis for improving this capability. However, without a common framework for comparing peak shapes and noise statistics, universal features of peak-parameter precision remain difficult to distinguish from those specific to a profile or noise regime, thereby hindering the development of general guidance for peak fitting and measurement design. Here we analyze Gaussian, Lorentzian, and pseudo-Voigt profiles in the Gaussian-noise (GN) limit using the same information-theoretic parameterization established for the Poisson-noise (PN) limit, enabling direct comparisons across peak shapes and noise regimes. Using the Fisher information matrix and the Cramér–Rao inequality, we derive analytical lower bounds on the standard deviations of peak intensity (I), center (ωc), full width at half maximum (Γ), area (A), and mixing parameter (η) and validate them against numerical calculations and Monte Carlo simulations. This unified framework addresses a long-standing question in peak analysis: whether intensity ratios or area ratios can be estimated more precisely. Whereas PN-limit theory predicts greater precision for area ratios across all three profiles, our GN-limit analysis shows that this advantage disappears for Gaussian and Lorentzian profiles and reverses for a pseudo-Voigt model with free η. Thus, neither I- nor A-based quantification is intrinsically more precise; their relative precision is governed by peak shape, parameter covariance, and noise statistics. This helps explain why experimental comparisons have not yielded a unique answer and provides a principled basis for selecting the more precise quantity. Fisher-information densities further show that information on I is concentrated in the peak core, information on ωc is concentrated on the flanks, and information on Γ and η extends into the wings. This indicates that precise estimation of Γ and η requires the fitting range to extend sufficiently into the peak wings. Finally, using Raman spectroscopy as an example, we combine the theory with detector-noise models to predict attainable precision before data acquisition and quantify how measurement conditions and instrument performance affect precision. The framework supports quantitative optimization of measurement conditions and instrument design to improve analytical precision across diverse signal-analysis applications.
items.authors: Yuuki Hagiwara, Tatsu Kuwatani

items.title: The Oxidation of Drug Molecules Using the Peroxygenase Activity of a Bacterial Family of Cytochrome P450 Enzymes
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes with peroxygenase activity can use H2O2 as the sole oxidant which is beneficial for biocatalytic applications. We investigated the peroxygenase activity of CYP105D18 from Streptomyces laurentii. The modification of the acid-alcohol pair in the I-helix through protein engineering reduced the peroxygenase activity for papaverine oxidation by 6-fold compared to the wild-type (WT) enzyme. We identified the oxidation metabolites as papaverine N-oxide, and two newly identified metabolites that arise from O-demethylation. The major O-demethylation metabolite was characterized as 6-O-desmethyl papaverine. Given the higher peroxygenase activity of the unmodified CYP105D18 enzyme we explored if another enzyme from the same CYP subfamily had similar activity. We produced and purified CYP105D41 from Streptomyces thermoviolaceus and found that this enzyme also has significant peroxygenase activity. CYP105D41 could catalyze the oxidation of papaverine and diclofenac. For this enzyme the oxidation of diclofenac was the more efficient reaction and generated 4′-hydroxydiclofenac, 5-hydroxydiclofenac and a doubly hydroxylated metabolite. Overall, we demonstrate that two CYP105 enzymes are effective natural peroxygenase biocatalysts and could efficiently oxidize drug molecules to generate human drug metabolites. These drug molecules are also emerging contaminants, and their oxidation would facilitate their removal from or breakdown in the environment.
items.authors: Tuhin Das, Shaun T. Ellis, Stephen G. Bell

items.title: Tautomeric Diversity in the Baicalein Radical Cation: EPR Fingerprints of a Traditional Chinese Medicine Antioxidant
items.abstract: The radical cation of baicalein, the principal bioactive flavonoid of the Traditional Chinese Medicine herb Scutellaria baicalensis, has been predicted to undergo an intramolecular proton transfer from the 5-hydroxyl to the 4carbonyl oxygen. This tautomerization produces two distinct electronic configurations, denoted C1 (canonical) and C2 (proton-transferred), whose relative populations and reactivities may determine the antioxidant behavior of the molecule within the single-electron-transfer–proton-transfer (SET-PT) pathway. The two tautomers have not, however, been distinguished experimentally; their UV-Vis signatures differ only subtly. Here we report the first EPR hyperfine fingerprints of the two tautomers, computed at the DFT/UM06-2X/EPR-III level across fourteen media. Three qualitatively distinct signatures separate C1 from C2 (values in water): a near-doubling of the isotropic coupling at the 5-hydroxyl oxygen O5 (from −5.88 to −11.77 G), a sign reversal at the aromatic carbon C5 (from +4.83 to −5.77 G), and the disappearance of the mobile proton’s coupling (from −3.49 to +0.30 G). All three qualitative signatures are preserved across dielectric constants from 1 to 78, making them robust diagnostics of the tautomeric state in a wide range of environments. Because EPR hyperfine couplings report directly on spin density rather than on electronic transitions, they provide an unambiguous experimental handle for detecting the tautomeric diversity of the baicalein radical cation.
items.authors: Ioan Bâldea, Ioan Baldea

items.title: Internal conversion in functionalized poly-chlorinated trityl radicals can be tuned by a characteristic high-frequency mode
items.abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of trends in radiative losses by internal conversion (IC) in a series of doublet radical emitters and triplet diradicals derived from the poly-chlorinated trityl moiety. Minimizing radiative losses in these systems by molecular design is of current interest to opto-electronics and quantum technological approaches. Our results clearly indicate that IC in the doublet emitters as well as in different diradical architectures is governed by a characteristic high-frequency mode, which is associated with a quinoidal distortion. For the doublet emitters, we can establish that deliberate design allows to deactivate this mode as decay channel, resulting in a significantly reduced IC rate and an improved internal fluorescence quantum yield. We propose an analogous design principle for highly fluorescent triplet diradicals, and discuss the role of a high fluorescence efficiency in the context of quantum applications.
items.authors: Robert Toews, Andreas Köhn

items.title: Time-Resolved Raman Spectroscopy of Nitrate Electroreduction Reveals Dynamic Interfacial Adsorbate Evolution
items.abstract: Nitrate electroreduction offers a pathway for coupling wastewater remediation with sustainable ammonia production, yet its mechanistic details under operating conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we directly resolve the dynamic evolution of nitrate-derived intermediates at electrified interfaces, addressing a key limitation in understanding dynamic reaction pathways. We employ time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TR-SERS) to monitor the interfacial behavior of NO 3 – and NO 2 – during nitrate reduction on roughened silver electrodes and observe potential-dependent vibrational shifts attributed to systematic changes in adsorption modes under increasingly cathodic potentials. Density functional theory calculations further support the vibrational assignments and provide insight into preferred binding motifs across the applied potential range. By tracking the time evolution of adsorbates, this approach provides insights into the sequence of adsorption and transformation steps on silver. The combined experimental and computational analysis contributes to a molecular-level understanding of nitrate electroreduction and provides a framework for probing dynamic reaction intermediates in nitrogen conversion electrocatalysis.
items.authors: Gabriel Floriano Costa, Jaxiry Barroso-Martinez, Dídac Armand Fenoll Silvestre, Connor Brennan-Pollak, Max García-Melchor, María Escudero-Escribano

items.title: Chemical Generalization Boundaries in Fire-Extinction Prediction from a Public Surfactant Formulation Database
items.abstract: Machine-learning models of firefighting surfactants can appear persuasive when repeated measurements or closely related formulations occur on both sides of a random split. We reconstructed the public Hinnant surfactant workbook at cell-level provenance and evaluated fire extinction with explicit failure labels and a hierarchy of increasingly stringent chemical splits. The reconstructed data contain 917 heptane and 595 gasoline fire tests; heptane extinction comprised 733 successes, 179 documented failures, and 5 unlabeled observations, whereas gasoline comprised 554 successes and 41 failures. Structure-based analyses retained 114 formulations built from 50 single-structure and 22 polydisperse represented materials. For the fixed Extra Trees/combined representation, pooled heptane success ROC–AUC was 0.812 for row-random, 0.813 for replicate-disjoint, 0.805 for formulation-disjoint, and 0.783 for component-set-disjoint evaluation. At the prespecified 0.55 Tanimoto stress threshold, 114 formulations formed seven families of sizes 87, 11, 10, 3, 1, 1, and 1; only five families had labeled heptane observations. A fixed FireSuppressionFP/Extra Trees leave-one-family-out stress test gave pooled ROC–AUC 0.557. The three unique historical family partitions gave macro, size-weighted, and pooled ROC–AUC values of 0.694, 0.572, and 0.557, respectively; model-seed repeats were not counted as independent partitions. Extinction-time prediction remained limited: formulation-disjoint MAE was 38.9 s with pooled R2 0.306, while the family stress test yielded MAE 45.8 s and pooled R2 0.076; the partition-macro family R2 was -0.105. Thus, extinction success generalized across unseen formulations and component sets within represented chemistry, but coarse-family extrapolation was unstable and poorly constrained. Results are retrospective associations for 19 cm liquid-pool fires, not prospective validation or evidence of wildland-fire performance.
items.authors: Aris Tsai

items.title: Direct Access to α-Chiral Amino-Oxetanes via Boron-Assisted Aziridine Ring-Opening
items.abstract: α-Chiral amino-oxetanes represent a high-value yet synthetically difficult to access scaffold class in medicinal chemistry, combining the favorable pharmacokinetic properties of the oxetane ring with an additional degree of molecular complexity and three-dimensionality. Here we report the first synthetic route to α-chiral amino-oxetanes bearing boron and silicon substituents via a boron-assisted aziridine ring-opening strategy. Treatment of multichiral borylated and silylated oxetanyl-aziridines with simple carboxylic acids proceeds under mild, base-free conditions with full regio- and diastereoselectivity, affording densely functionalized products in excellent yields. The methodology accommodates over 30 structurally diverse carboxylic acids, including complex building blocks and Nprotected amino acids, and extends to azetidine analogs in a scalable protocol. Mechanistic investigations combining density functional theory computations and kinetic studies reveal a novel boron-assisted activation mode: reversible proton transfer from the carboxylic acid to the aziridine nitrogen generates a reactive aziridinium/carboxylate ion pair, which undergoes rate-determining SN2 attack facilitated by boron-oxygen coordination, lowering the activation barrier by more than 10 kcal·mol-1. This work expands the boron- and silicon-enriched chemical space accessible for drug discovery while simultaneously establishing a versatile platform for the synthesis of densely functionalized, stereochemically complex amino-oxetane scaffolds.
items.authors: Lucie S. Eisen, Mireia Pujol, Volker Derdau, Elena Fernández, Enrique Gomez-Bengoa, Maria Mendez

items.title: Product Accelerated Photodegradation of Nitro-Spirothiopyrans
items.abstract: The long term stability of conjugated fluorescent and photochromic compounds is essential for their application in materials and devices, but is often highly sensitive to changes in molecular structure. This aspect is particularly prominent in the 6'-nitro-spiropyran and 6'-nitro-spirothiopyran photochromes, which differ only in a O/S atom at the spiro center but show remarkably different stability under UV irradiation. Here, we show, using femtosecond and nanosecond transient absorption and NIR emission spectroscopy supported by quantum chemical calculations, that from a photo-physical and -chemical perspective the two compounds are remarkably similar. Time-resolved NIR emission of 1 O 2 , gas chromatography and NMR spectroscopy, reveal that the difference in observed photostability is due to the greater quantum yield for 1 O 2 generation of the photodegradation products in the case of NSTP .
items.authors: Andy S. Sardjan, Ruben Feringa, Wybren Jan Buma, Denis Jacquemin, Wesley R. Browne

items.title: Assigning the Low-Energy Excitons in Far-Red Photosystem II through Atomistic Modeling
items.abstract: Far-red light photoacclimation of cyanobacteria extends the spectral range of oxygenic photosynthesis through the incorporation of chlorophylls (Chls) d and f into natural Photosystems, but the energetic organization of these pigments remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electronic-structure calculations with atomistic QM/MM and polarizable QM/MM approaches to determine the site energies, electronic couplings, and excitonic structure of the far-red PSII from Synechococcus sp. PCC 7335. In particular, we use benchmark calculations against spin-component-scaled CC2 to assess the accuracy of long-range corrected density functionals for describing the relative energetics of Chls a, d and f. Our calculations reveal that the energetic tuning of the far-red pigments is governed primarily by protein electrostatics, whereas structural distortions and environmental polarization make comparatively minor contributions. We found significant excitonic interactions within the subset of CP47 chlorophylls, while the reaction-center Chl d remains largely localized. The resulting excitonic Hamiltonian quantitatively reproduces both the far-red absorption spectrum and the sequence of exciton energies extracted from two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy, enabling a first-principles assignment of the low-energy excitons to specific Chl f and Chl d pigments. These results provide an atomistic picture of the far-red excitonic landscape and establish a quantitative basis for future simulations of excitation-energy transfer and charge separation in far-red photosystems.
items.authors: Samuele Giannini, Luca Ancillotti, Lorenzo Cupellini

items.title: In silico evaluation of novel isosteres against PTPN1 and estrogen receptor alpha: molecular docking, ADMET profiling, and quantum chemical analysis
items.abstract: A series of novel cyclic alkene template (CAT) isosteres (CAT-0 to CAT-7) were designed and evaluated through an integrated in silico workflow combining molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT) based electronic structure analysis, ADMET prediction, CYP450 profiling, and preliminary synthetic feasibility assessment. Two biologically relevant protein targets, protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTPN1) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα/ESR1), were investigated to explore the potential biological activity profiles of the designed compounds. Docking studies were performed using the 2HNP and 3ERT crystal structures for PTPN1 and ERα, respectively. Validation of the docking protocols through reproduction of the corresponding co-crystallized ligand poses yielded RMSD values below 2 Å, supporting the reliability of the docking procedures. CAT-3, CAT-4, and CAT-7 were identified as the most promising candidates based on their predicted binding affinities across the two targets. Electronic structure analysis suggested that variations in electrostatic potential distribution and frontier orbital characteristics may contribute to differences in binding behavior within the series, supporting the isosteric design strategy. ADMET and toxicity predictions indicated generally favorable drug-like properties, with most compounds exhibiting acceptable gastrointestinal absorption and low predicted CYP450 inhibitory activity, suggesting a limited risk of CYP-mediated drug–drug interactions. However, variability in blood–brain barrier permeability and model-dependent toxicity endpoints highlights the inherent uncertainty of in silico ADMET predictions and warrants cautious interpretation of absolute values. Among the designed compounds, CAT-3 emerged as the most balanced lead candidate, combining favorable docking performance, acceptable predicted pharmacokinetic properties, and improved synthetic accessibility relative to CAT-4 and CAT-7, which, despite strong predicted affinities, present greater synthetic constraints. Its structural relationship to trodusquemine further supports its relevance as a promising scaffold. Overall, CAT-3 represents the most favorable compromise between predicted biological activity and practical feasibility within the series. Nevertheless, given the limitations of empirical scoring functions, rigid receptor approximations, and predictive ADMET models, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Further validation through molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA free energy calculations, and experimental assays will be required to confirm the predicted biological relevance of the CAT series.
items.authors: Lilian Rouille

items.title: PervoTransformer: Multi-Scale Transformer-Based Device Design and Atomistic Modeling of Perovskites
items.abstract: Perovskite solar cell design involves a large and highly coupled space of material compositions, layer structures, and physical parameters, making systematic exploration of complete device architectures computationally challenging. This work introduces PervoTransformer, a transformer-based framework that represents complete device architectures as sequences and learns device-level behavior directly from this representation. A RoBERTa model is fine-tuned on SCAPS-generated device sequences spanning six perovskite families, including MAPbI3, FAPbI3, CsPbI3, and their Sn-based analogs. The model simultaneously predicts multiple performance metrics, including power conversion efficiency (PCE), short-circuit current density (Jsc), open-circuit voltage (Voc), and fill factor (FF), demonstrating the ability of transformer encoders to capture coupled, nonlinear dependencies across complete device stacks. To explore configurations beyond the training distribution, a GPT-2 model is fine-tuned using the same device-sequence representation to generate candidate architectures with new combinations of compositional and physical parameters. Generated configurations are screened for validity and uniqueness and subsequently evaluated using the fine-tuned RoBERTa model, enabling efficient exploration of under-sampled regions of the device design space. In parallel, machine-learned interatomic potentials based on the MACE framework are fine-tuned for CsSnX3 (X = Cl,Br, I) using available DFT data, enabling efficient structural relaxation and exploration of lead-free Sn-based perovskites. The resulting multiscale framework combines sequence-based transformer models for device-level design with machine-learned interatomic potentials for atomistic materials exploration, while retaining first-principles calculations for detailed physical validation. This approach provides a scalable strategy for navigating the coupled materials and device design spaces of perovskite solar cells while reducing reliance on computationally expensive simulations during initial exploration.
items.authors: Wahid Hussain, Ali Hamza, Muhammad Sultan, Fouzia Perveen Malik

items.title: Coherent Recrossing Challenges Mechanistic Interpretations from Surface Hopping
items.abstract: Surface hopping is widely used to assign mechanisms in ultrafast molecular photodynamics, yet the resulting mechanistic picture can become strongly method-dependent when electronic coherence survives across recurrent nonadiabatic interactions. We identify this regime, which can arise in dense excited-state manifolds, as coherent recrossing. Using semiclassical analysis of the prototypical Tully dual avoided-crossing model, we disentangle three controlling ingredients: phase accumulation between nonadiabatic events, electronic decoherence, and the relative phase information encoded in the nonadiabatic coupling. We then examine [3.3]paracyclophane, comparing surface hopping with ab initio multiple spawning (AIMS) using the same Hamiltonian, initial conditions, and coupling treatment. AIMS predicts prolonged multistate population sharing with state-selective electronic coherence, whereas the tested surface-hopping variants yield dynamics qualitatively distinct from AIMS. Landau–Zener surface hopping (LZSH) does not propagate electronic amplitudes and consequently cannot retain phase memory between successive nonadiabatic events, preventing it from describing interference that depends on such memory. Fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) and local-diabatization surface hopping (LDSH), with and without standard decoherence correction, reveal a fourth controlling ingredient that emerges in the multistate regime: the state-pair selectivity of the retained coherence. The tested FSSH and LDSH treatments retain coherence less selectively than AIMS and fail to reproduce its population dynamics, ranging from rapid S1 funneling to excessively broad population sharing. However, because FSSH and LDSH propagate electronic amplitudes and therefore retain phase information, their description of coherent recrossing can in principle be improved through more appropriate treatments of decoherence.
items.authors: Juan Alberto Guzman Abrego, Anik Mukhopadhyay, Rafael S. Mattos, Josene M. Toldo, Mario Barbatti

items.title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in 2025: The certified frontier held while verification stayed scarce
items.abstract: This review assembles the complete 12-month publication record retrospectively, rather than through sequential monthly monitoring. The corpus holds 7931 publications meeting the topical scope criteria, of which 450 were examined in close detail across date-resolved monthly cohorts, alongside 1089 publications dated only to the calendar year. Within this literature, only 66 investigations reported an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE), which peaked at 33.15% for the year. Certified values moved from 30.26% in the first month recording a verified metric to 30.1% in the last, a net displacement of-0.16. Buried contact modification with carbazole self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), low-dimensional capping heterostructures, and additive-directed crystallization drove the performance records in both monolithic tandem and single-junction architectures. Mechanistic consensus breaks down over whether these surface modifiers permanently eliminate deep electronic traps or merely impose transient electrostatic potential shifts. Several groups attribute suppressed non-radiative recombination and stabilized open-circuit voltage (Voc) to chemical defect healing, while competing investigations demonstrate that asymmetric interfacial dipoles create electrostatic crosstalk, transport barriers, and unshielded internal fields that accelerate halide segregation. Carrying these interfacial treatments to scalable modules incurs a severe area penalty, with sharp efficiency deficits as aperture dimensions expand toward the maximum reported area of 764 cm2. In blade and slot-die deposition, the molecular attributes that minimize interface recombination in spin-coated cells directly impair meniscus translation, because hydrophobic self-assembled monolayer (SAM) terminal groups form precursor micellar aggregates that induce solvent dewetting, pinhole formation, and lateral nucleation gradients across wide substrates. Operational stability data remain deficient across the publication record. Merely 15 studies documented operational lifetimes, the longest reaching 3200 h, and only 24 articles followed standardized International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) procedures. Most stability assessments evaluated unencapsulated storage in inert atmospheres, or omitted continuous maximum power point tracking (MPPT) under elevated operating temperatures, which leaves lifetime projections uncalibrated against operational degradation modes. Abstract-level reporting frequencies confirm the same verification gap: statements of independent certification occurred in just 5.8% of evaluated abstracts across the year, varying between 3.4% and 7.6% across monthly cohorts. Champion efficiency claims therefore rest predominantly on unverified, small-area laboratory cells that remain susceptible to spectral mismatch and calibration artifacts. Read across device architectures, the high open-circuit voltages obtained through contact engineering are frequently purchased with accelerated chemical and electronic degradation. Phosphonic acid anchor groups corrode reactive nickel oxide hole-transport layers under operating bias, and low-dimensional perovskite capping overlayers introduce anisotropic out-of-plane transport barriers that accumulate photogenerated carriers, lowering the kinetic activation barrier for electricfield-driven halide migration and phase demixing. In narrow-bandgap tin-lead absorbers, evidence settling whether stannous oxidation stems from autonomous chemical redox reactions or from downstream lattice microstrain remains thin, since chemical reducing agents delay degradation without resolving the underlying mechanical distortion. Establishing whether passivating molecules permanently eliminate deep recombination centers, or merely raise temporary barriers that disguise latent operational instabilities, requires synchronized operando spectroscopic and impedance measurements under simultaneous electrical bias and thermal stress.
items.authors: Havid Aqoma

items.title: A transcriptional reporting system for sensing interactions of small molecules with proteins
items.abstract: Characterizing binding interactions of small molecules with proteins is important in many areas of chemistry and biology. We show here that a transcriptional activation sequence from Escherichia Coli (E. Coli) can be exploited to create a binding sensor for small molecule/protein interactions. The system requires two key components: small molecules connected to a DNA bearing a transcriptional activation sequence (TAS) and proteins of interest (POIs) expressed as fusions with the transcriptional activation domain (TAD) from the phage shock protein F (PspF). If the DNA bound small molecule binds to the POI, the induced proximity of the TAD to the TAS initiates transcription, with the number of copies of RNA produced proportional to the binding affinity. Although numerous direct binding measurement techniques are known, very few of these amplify binding signals, or convert the binding signal to a different molecular form which is then easy to handle and quantify. We demonstrate several use cases where the technique will prove valuable, such as in characterizing binders, identifying molecular glues, or as a reporter in DNA encoded library (DEL) selections.
items.authors: Koder Dagher, Minqi Pan, Basilius Sauter, Saule Zhanybekova, Pinwen Cai, Lukas Schneider

items.title: Accelerating the Discovery of Marine Natural Products with Antimicrobial activity via Bioactivity-Driven Molecular Networking
items.abstract: The growing threat of antimicrobial resistance underscores an urgent need to investigate underexplored natural sources to provide new chemical scaffolds for drug development. Marine environments, particularly those along the South African coastline, represent reservoirs of novel chemical diversity with the potential to provide new classes of antibiotics. This study reports the development of an efficient biodiscovery pipeline for the assembly and systematic screening of marine natural products extract libraries to identify novel antimicrobial leads. The workflow integrates microbial genomics and biological screening with non-targeted high resolution tandem mass spectrometry and molecular networking. Chemical extracts of 174 sponges and tunicates collected from the South African coast were evaluated for antibacterial, cytotoxic, and in vitro enzyme inhibitory activity. Guided by molecular networkbased feature prioritization, eleven known secondary metabolites spanning four major 2 structural classes (bifunctional sphingolipids, variabilin furanosesterterpenes, topsentin bisindole and pyrrolo iminoquinone -alkaloids) were isolated. The bioactivity of the isolated compounds was consistent with their corresponding crude extracts. Computational mass spectrometry analysis of extracts with antimicrobial activity revealed additional enriched metabolite families warranting further investigation. Finally, we profiled the taxonomic diversity of sponge associated bacterial communities to assess their utility in facilitating dereplication and prioritization of species of interest for further study.
items.authors: Jarmo-Charles J Kalinski, Tarryn Swart, Idris Njanje, Gabriella Solomons, Dele Abdissa Keneni, Shirley Parker-Nance

items.title: Finding the Right TEMPO: Multi-Objective Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of TEMPO Derivatives for Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Catholytes
items.abstract: We formulate the discovery of aqueous redox flow battery catholytes as a multi-objective optimization problem and introduce a virtual screening framework that simultaneously considers redox potential, chemical stability, and synthetic accessibility. Applied to a library of 182 TEMPO derivatives, the workflow identified a diverse set of high-ranking candidates, including the previously unexplored methyl carbamate-TEMPO (MC-TEMPO) and diethylamino-TEMPO (DEA-TEMPO). Furthermore, the screening revealed a moderate correlation between redox potential and predicted degradation resistance, indicating an intrinsic trade-off between these properties. For established TEMPO derivatives, the framework reproduced relative performance trends reported within independently studied series. Across the broader library, the highest-ranked candidates reflected a non-intuitive balance of electrochemical performance, stability, and synthetic accessibility rather than optimization of redox potential alone. MC-TEMPO and DEA-TEMPO were subsequently synthesized and experimentally characterized, providing a prospective test of the computational predictions. Cyclic voltammetry validated the redox potential predictions, with measured values closely matching the calculated values. During 130 h potentiostatic holds under sustained oxidizing conditions, MC-TEMPO showed no measurable electrochemical or molecular degradation, whereas DEA-TEMPO underwent a substituent-specific degradation pathway not captured by the initial screening model. Together, these results show that multi-objective catholyte discovery can prioritize molecules that would be overlooked by redox-potential optimization alone and provides a framework for the computationally guided design of organic redox flow battery catholytes.
items.authors: Daniel Willimetz, Žak Ruben Šinkovec, Jan Hamaekers, Alexei Lapkin, Abhishek Khetan

items.title: TKitOC PRO v8+: An Interactive Cloud-Based Platform Integrating Target Discovery and Chemoinformatics Workflows
items.abstract: The transition from biological target identification to structure-based molecular analysis commonly requires researchers to combine multiple software environments, file formats, and external web services. This fragmentation can increase preprocessing effort and create practical barriers for computational biology education and early-stage in silico research. Here, we present TKitOC PRO v8+, an interactive cloud-based platform designed to integrate sequence analysis, molecular diagnostics, structural data preparation, and chemoinformatics workflows within a unified graphical interface deployed through Google Colab. The platform unifies the in silico workflow by distributing functionalities across 13 modular tabs organized into two core pipelines. The Target Discovery and Molecular Diagnostics pipeline provides nucleotide and protein sequence processing, open reading frame analysis across six frames, codonpreference back-translation, automated primer design through Primer3, in silico primer specificity assessment using NCBI BLASTn, and protein functional annotation via InterPro coupled with an immediate local motif-based Fast-Track algorithm. The Structure and Chemoinformatics pipeline integrates molecular descriptor calculation through RDKit, structural visualization with py3Dmol, ligand extraction and format preparation, and automated assembly of receptor–ligand complexes via DockPrime from externally generated docking outputs. As a proof-of-concept case study, we applied the platform to the KPC-2 carbapenemase—a critical antimicrobial resistance determinant from the ESKAPE group—using the crystallographic structure PDB 2OV5. The workflow started from the deposited protein sequence, verified taxonomic identity via BLASTn identified the Class Aβ-lactamase target, generated a corresponding nucleotide representation through back-translation, assessed sequence correspondence through BLASTn, generated candidate primer pairs targeting the blaKPC gene, and connected the resulting target characterization with functional annotation and structural analysis. The resulting workflow demonstrates how TKitOC PRO v8+ can reduce manual transitions between heterogeneous computational tools and provide an accessible environment for bioinformatics and chemoinformatics training and preliminary research workflows.
items.authors: Angel Eduardo Nava-Saldivar, Jonnathan Guadalupe Santillán-Benítez

items.title: Enantioselective Strain-Release Formal (3 + 3) Cycloaddition of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to Chiral 1,4-Diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Relay Dy/Ir Catalysis
items.abstract: *Email: nowmiracle@zjnu.edu.cn; dengwp827@zjnu.edu.cn ABSTRACT: Pyrazines and piperazines are privileged 1,4-diaza motifs, yet neither combines conformational rigidity with a stereochemically defined three-dimensional shape. Here we report the first catalytic enantioselective formal (3 + 3) cycloaddition of 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), providing direct access to enantioenriched 1,4diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes—rigid, C(sp3)-rich scaffolds that serve as chiral three-dimensional complements to these classical motifs. Relay Dy/Ir catalysis merges Dy(OTf)3-promoted ABB strain release with iridium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic amination of allylamine-derived N,C,C synthons, extending ABB chemistry beyond conventional strain-release functionalization and previously reported racemic cycloadditions. The method furnishes 50 examples in up to 93% yield and 99% ee, with broad functional-group tolerance and compatibility with drug- and natural-product-derived substrates. Control experiments, 1H NMR studies, and DFT calculations support a staged mechanism involving carbonyl-assisted N,O-bidentate activation of the ABB by Dy(OTf)3. Preparative-scale synthesis, orthogonal product diversification, and access to pyrazineand piperazine-related drug analogues demonstrate the synthetic versatility and scaffold-hopping potential of this platform.
items.authors: Jun-Cheng Jin, Jian Zhang, Qi-Guo Zheng, Hanliang Zheng, Wei-Ping Deng

items.title: Microstate-Aware Excited-State Descriptors Improve Scaffold-Robust Prediction of Drug Phototoxicity
items.abstract: Drug phototoxicity depends on electronically excited states whose energies and intensities can change with protonation, tautomerism, and conformation, yet most predictive models represent a single parent structure. We evaluated a molecular-state-aware workflow on a curated 450-compound in vitro photoirritation (PIV) benchmark expanded to 1,088 microstates. Across 10 repeated 5-fold scaffold-held-out cross-validations, mean ROC-AUC increased from 0.745 for structure alone to 0.792 after adding parent xTB+sTDA descriptors, 0.807 with microstate summaries, and 0.808 with conformer aggregation; PR-AUC increased from 0.669 to 0.727. Compound-paired bootstrap analysis gave a full-model ROC-AUC gain of +0.0569 (95% CI 0.0234-0.0908) and PR-AUC gain of +0.0533 (0.0133-0.0933). Higher-level Q-Chem calculations preserved screening excited-state ordering (S1 Pearson r = 0.946; T1 r = 0.931), and an additional preselected state panel completed 22/24 TDA jobs with all four parent-alternate microstate pairs available. These pairs showed substantial state-dependent changes, including a 240.4 to 259.0 nm bright-state shift for trinexapac-ethyl. Clinical PIH endpoint transfer was modest (n = 155; ROC-AUC 0.609), consistent with endpoint and chemical-space shift. The results support molecular-state-aware excited-state featurization as a mechanistically grounded strategy for computational photosafety.
items.authors: Aris Tsai

items.title: Health risk assessment of carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic heavy metal exposure from commercial instant noodles in Bangladesh: a deterministic and probabilistic evaluation for adults and children
items.abstract: The contribution of the instant noodle cake itself to dietary heavy metal exposure in Bangladesh has not been quantified. Nine metals (Pb, Cd, Cr, Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, Ni and Co) were determined by flame atomic absorption spectrometry in eight leading brands (102 packets) from Dhaka, Rajshahi and Khulna, seasoning sachet excluded. The hazard index (HI) and total cancer risk (TCR) were estimated for adults and children at national-average (0.36 g day -1 ) and high-consumption (25.6 g day -1 ) ingestion rates, with uncertainty propagated by bootstrap Monte Carlo simulation. Mean concentrations ranged from 17.7 mg kg -1 (Fe) to 0.030 mg kg -1 (Cd), and all brands complied with the Codex and Bangladeshi limits for Pb, Cd and Ni. No THQ exceeded 1; HI was 0.003 (adults) and 0.010 (children) at average intake and 0.19 and 0.71 at high intake, with Co contributing half of the HI. TCR was tolerable (10 -6 to 10 -4 ) at average intake but reached 9.8 × 10 -5 for high consuming adults and 3.7 × 10 -4 for high-consuming children, exceeding 10 -4 in 34% and 83% of simulations; Ni and Cr accounted for 95% of the cancer risk. Regulatory compliance therefore does not ensure negligible risk for frequent child consumers, and the risk-driving metals are those without a maximum level. Comparison with studies of noodles analyzed with their sachets indicates that the sachet, not the cake, is the main Pb source. Risk-based surveillance of Cr, Ni and Co, harmonization of the national standard with Codex, and control of sachet ingredients are recommended.
items.authors: Debneela Paul, Sagar Bhowmik, Sheikh Mohiuddin Samrat, Sayed M. A. Salam

items.title: Solid-state Electron Transfer Mechanism Study in Mechanochemistry through Time-Resolved Multimodal Monitoring
items.abstract: Mechanochemical reactions can access unusual and useful reactivity, but the electron-transfer steps that govern many of these mechanochemical transformations have remained difficult for time-resolved monitoring. Here we establish a time-resolved strategy for resolving mechanochemical electron transfer by integrating in-situ powder X-ray diffraction with ex-situ quantitative electron paramagnetic resonance, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance, and magnetometry. Using the formation of a sodium anion complex (sodide) as a model reaction, we show that a mechanically driven disproportionation proceeds through a stepwise pathway involving an electride intermediate. This finding provides direct mechanistic insight into how electrons move through reactive solids under mechanochemical condition. More broadly, it establishes a general experimental blueprint for identifying electronically distinct transient intermediates in mechanochemical redox chemistry.
items.authors: Huanxin Zhang, Nathan Davison, Tomislav Stolar, Floriana Tuna, Conrad A. P. Goodwin, Franziska Emmerling

items.title: In-column Synthesis and Atomic-resolution Electron Microscopic Analysis of Metastable Reactive Nitrides
items.abstract: Metastable and air-sensitive compounds are challenging to synthesize and characterize because their formation often requires harsh conditions and their structures can rapidly evolve upon exposure to the environment. Here, we demonstrate that a high-vacuum environment inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) column can serve simultaneously as a reaction platform and an atomic-scale analytical tool for generating and interrogating such materials. Electron-beam irradiation on sodium azide (NaN3) produces crystalline sodium nitride (Na3N) at room temperature, despite the conventional decomposition of NaN3 into sodium and nitrogen. The formation of Na3N is supported by high-resolution TEM, electron diffraction, and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, which reveal correlated structural and compositional changes through irradiation. The resulting Na3N subsequently undergoes oxidation through an amorphous intermediate to form polycrystalline Na2O. The high-vacuum environment sufficiently suppresses this reaction to resolve its otherwise unachievable microscopic mechanisms. Extending this approach to potassium azide (KN3), we observe a transient crystalline phase that is most consistently indexed as K3N, a nitride known to be thermally unstable even under room temperature. Its transient appearance and decay indicate a dynamic balance between electron-beam-induced formation and degradation. These results establish in-column electron-beam chemistry as a route to metastable nitride formation while enabling multimodal characterization of highly reactive products. More broadly, this strategy offers a means of exploring nonequilibrium metastable compounds that are difficult to access using conventional synthesis and characterization workflows.
items.authors: Masaya Sakakibara, Koji Harano, Ryusei Kudo, Jun Kawano, Tomoya Yamazaki, Yuki Kimura

items.title: Acoustic-assisted HDX-MS for Intact Virion Analysis
items.abstract: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) enables solution-phase characterization of protein interactions and conformational dynamics, but analysis of intact enveloped virions remains challenging because limited proteolytic accessibility restricts peptide recovery. Here, we developed an acoustic-assisted HDX-MS workflow integrating chemical denaturation with bath sonication during quenching and applied it to dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV2) strain D2Y98P. The workflow achieved sequence coverages of 96.0 ± 0.7%, 89.8 ± 0.8% and 87.1 ± 1.0% for the capsid (C), envelope (E) and membrane (M) proteins, respectively. Model peptide measurements showed comparable back-exchange between sonication and incubation at matched durations, although longer treatment increased deuterium loss. Improved E protein coverage enabled characterization of changes in deuterium uptake associated with binding of the neutralizing antibody 2D22. Protected regions overlapped spatially with the cryo-EM-defined quaternary interface, while additional protection occurred in regions remote from direct antibody contact. These findings are consistent with antibody-associated conformational stabilization extending beyond the binding interface. Acoustic-assisted HDX-MS therefore improves structural protein coverage and complements cryo-EM by revealing peptide-level changes in antibodyassociated protein dynamics in the intact virion context.
items.authors: Li Ching Pang, Ying Deng, Vinayak Gupta, Wen Zheng Lo, Shuangshuang Zhu, Muen Shan

items.title: Polyanion-Based Compounds for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
items.abstract: Rechargeable magnesium metal batteries represent a compelling post-lithium energy storage technology owing to the abundance of terrestrial magnesium reserves, their current cost-effectiveness and intrinsically higher safety relative to lithium systems, coupled with their capacity to deliver high volumetric energy density. However, this promise and beyond remains constrained by the stringent requirement that rapid and reversible Mg 2+ transport can be achieved in concert with electrochemical and thermodynamic stability across both electrodes and electrolytes. Within this context, polyanion compounds, such as phosphates, silicates, and borates, have emerged as a pedagogically rich and technologically versatile class of materials. Polyanion-based compounds offer high redox voltages, exceptional thermal and chemical robustness, and a plethora of crystallographic chemistries that permit rational tuning of Mg 2+ migration pathways. This Review surveys polyanion-based positive electrodes and solid electrolytes for rechargeable magnesium batteries, with emphasis on computational prediction, mechanistic elucidation, synthetic methodology, advanced structural and spectroscopic characterisation, and the prospects for all- solid-state magnesium batteries capable of operating under high‑temperature conditions.
items.authors: Titus Masese, Godwill Mbiti Kanyolo

items.title: Overriding Intrinsic Regioselectivity in Propargylic Substitution via Cu/Pd Synergistic Catalysis for Enantioselective Dienylation
items.abstract: Propargylic substitution is a fundamental strategy in asymmetric catalysis for constructing enantioenriched unsaturated molecules, yet the dienylation pathway via nucleophilic attack at the central carbon of propargyl/allenyl-metal intermediates has remained elusive. Here we report that Cu/Pd synergistic catalysis enables the first catalytic asymmetric dienylation with broad carbon nucleophiles, delivering enantioenriched 1,3‑dienes with exceptional levels of regioselectivity ( 20:1), enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee), and E/Z selectivity ( 20:1). Mechanistic and DFT studies establish distinct roles for the two metals: palladium governs regiocontrol, while the chiral copper complex is responsible for enantioselectivity, enabling complementary dienylation with high regio- and enantioselectivity. Stronger palladium–terminal-carbon interactions make terminal attack energetically costly and direct the regioselective reaction to the central carbon of the π-propargyl-Pd complex, thereby overriding the inherent preference for propargylation and allenylation. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by diverse transformations of the enantioenriched diene products, thereby enabling the rapid assembly of complex molecular architectures. Beyond providing a general strategy for reprogramming the innate regioselectivity of π‑propargyl chemistry, this work highlights the potential of bimetallic synergistic catalysis as a practical platform for tackling long‑standing selectivity challenges in asymmetric synthesis.
items.authors: Yuxuan Shi, Yue Shi, Yun Zhang, Yongzhi Chen, Haowen Tang, Mengfu Dai

items.title: Thermodynamics and Accurate Solubilities of Lithium and Sodium Salts in Imidazolium-Based Ionic Liquids
items.abstract: Determining the solubility of metal salts in ionic liquids is challenging using visual methods or Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC). The slow crystallization kinetics of the metal salts impede accurate Solid-Liquid Equilibrium (SLE) measurements, resulting in significant discrepancies in the limited available literature. We propose Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) as an alternative technique to measure the solubility of metal salts in ionic liquids at different temperatures. Some new solubility data of lithium and sodium salts in imidazolium ionic liquid were determined. We show how the ITC experiments not only provide accurate solubility data at the studied temperatures but also reveal key thermodynamic properties of dissolution, including the enthalpy of dissolution; the mixing enthalpy and the partial molar excess enthalpy of both components at saturation.
items.authors: Guillaume Depraetère, Nithavong Cam, Agílio Pádua, Margarida Costa Gomes

items.title: Molecular Dynamics Studies of Model Ionizable Lipids in an mRNA Vaccine
items.abstract: Effective COVID-19 mRNA vaccines encapsulate nucleoside-modified messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA), which encodes the prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, inside lipid nanoparticles. Endosomal acidification motivates the study of ionizable lipid protonation. Here, we isolate how protonation changes hydration, solvent preference, and structural organization of ALC-0315 in simplified model environments. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we identify clear protonation-dependent differences in lipid orientation, hydration, and collective organization across three model systems. At a water/hexane interface, the protonated amine headgroup shows a stronger preference for the aqueous phase, reflecting enhanced interactions with water molecules. In 20-lipid assemblies, the protonated assembly remains more hydrated and aqueous-associated over the simulated trajectory, whereas the neutral assembly migrates toward and spreads along the water/hexane interface. In pure ALC-0315 bilayer simulations, protonation strengthens amine hydration and alters bilayer-scale structural organization, with the observed morphology depending on the pressure-coupling protocol. Collectively, these findings demonstrate how protonation of ionizable amine headgroups can remodel ALC-0315 assemblies through strengthened lipid–water interactions. These simplified systems provide molecular-level insight into protonation-dependent ALC-0315 behavior, while not directly modeling the full multicomponent LNP, the endosomal membrane, or mRNA release.
items.authors: Mohsen Farshad, Jayendran C. Rasaiah

items.title: Capturing the Effect of Exact Exchange in Thio-Michael Additions with a Machine-Learned Functional at Meta-GGA Cost
items.abstract: Semilocal density-functional approximations fail to describe the formation of anionic enolates in thio-Michael additions, the bond-forming step of covalent-inhibitor warheads; range-separated hybrids, which reintroduce long-range exact exchange, are required. Across the published CCSD(T)validated reaction pathways of eight warheads, we show that Skala—a deep-learned semilocal functional containing no exact exchange—matches the range-separated hybrid reference for the activation barriers, enolate geometries and relaxed reactant structures, outperforming the global hybrid B3LYP at meta-GGA cost. The one signature it does not reproduce is the orbital one: its Koopmans ionization potential stays at the semilocal scale, because the ionization-potential theorem constrains the exchange potential, not the energy. Skala thus captures the effect of exact exchange in the total energy, from training data alone.
items.authors: Connor Williamson, Ross Amory, David M. Rogers, Katherine Inzani, Jonathan D. Hirst

items.title: A Flexible Framework for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences
items.abstract: Course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) broaden access to the high-impact practice of undergraduate research. Unfortunately, many faculty lack a clear roadmap for developing a CURE. To address this barrier, we present a series of modular activities, the CURE "Flexi-Framework", which guides faculty through the process of creating a CURE based on their own research. Within the framework, students progress through four phases of scientific research: (I) Obtaining, Evaluating, and Organizing Information; (II) Asking Questions and Planning Investigations; (III) Investigation, Data Analysis, and Iteration; and (IV) Justification and Communication through a written report and/or oral presentation. Each phase consists of assessable, workshop-style activities that can be adapted to different research topics while maintaining the CURE-defining elements of collaboration, discovery and relevance, and iteration. Over the past decade, the Flexi-Framework has been used to implement multiple upper-division CUREs across three institutions and several subdisciplines of chemistry. Assessment using the Classroom Undergraduate Research Experience Survey and the Laboratory Course Assessment Survey demonstrates student-reported gains and course design elements consistent with national CURE benchmarks. The CURE Flexi-Framework thus provides a validated, adaptable pathway for integrating research into coursework, lowering the barrier to adopting CUREs across institutional and disciplinary contexts.
items.authors: Kathryn L. Haas, Jennifer Fishovitz, Michael J. Drummond, William C. Pfalzgraff, LeeAnn M. Sager-Smith

items.title: BULK VERSUS SURFACE CHARGE RECOMBINATION KINETICS IN POLYMER HETEROJUNCTION NANOPARTICLE PHOTOCATALYST DISPERSIONS
items.abstract: Organic donor-acceptor heterojunction nanoparticles have emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar hydrogen production, combining efficient light harvesting, donor-acceptor charge separation, and the generation of long-lived charge carriers. However, the identity of the charge populations responsible for photocatalytic turnover remains unresolved. Here, we study photogenerated polarons in aqueous oligo(ethylene glycol)-functionalized IDTBT:IDTBR-based heterojunction nanoparticles using transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) and photoinduced absorption spectroscopy (PIAS) to probe, respectively, the transient polarons generated under pulsed excitation and long-lived polarons that accumulate under continuous illumination. By directly correlating spectroscopic signatures with photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, we show that the steady-state PIAS response tracks photocatalytic activity, establishing long-lived accumulated charges as the reactive population governing photocatalytic turnover. Excitation-fluence studies further demonstrate that the contrasting TAS and PIAS responses originate from distinct trapped-charge populations, with decay times at matched charge densities being five orders of magnitude faster for TAS compared to PIAS. We attribute the exceptionally long lifetimes measured in PIAS to the synergistic effects of donor-acceptor charge separation, progressive trap filling under continuous illumination, and dielectric stabilisation provided by the aqueous glycol-functionalized environment, which together suppress charge recombination and enable long-lived charge accumulation under operating conditions. These findings identify operando PIAS as a powerful approach for probing catalytically relevant charge populations and provide mechanistic design principles for engineering organic semiconductor photocatalysts with enhanced solar fuel performance.
items.authors: Soranyel Gonzalez-Carrero, Jan Kosco, Chen Zhang, Michael Sachs, Teng Fei, Iain McCulloch

items.title: Testing for the presence of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals in Locally Available Perfumes in Pakistan Through GC-MS Analysis and Implications for Public Health Policy
items.abstract: Introduction Many conventional perfumes contain Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs) like phthalates, synthetic musk, and parabens – often hidden under the ingredient label ‘fragrance’ or ‘parfum.’ Daily exposure to EDCs, through inhalation and skin contact, is very harmful, resulting in multiple health issues in infants, children, and adolescents undergoing critical developmental stages. In Pakistan, consumers remain considerably unaware, making this a serious problem. Perfumes are typically produced by unauthorised local manufacturers who do not follow standard protocols. Local brands are not bound by any explicit ingredient labelling laws. Currently, little to no research is done in this area. Methods In the months of March to April 2026, four local perfumes were arbitrarily purchased from the Pakistani consumer market in Lahore. The four perfumes were de-identified them and randomly coded them from 1 to 4. The perfumes were sent to the Industrial Analytical Centre in Karachi and analysed qualitatively and quantitatively using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for EDCs. Results Analysis showed that four perfumes contained Citral, three contained hydroxycitronellal, two contained Benzyl Salicylate, and two contained Benzyl Benzoate: all of which are established, potent EDCs and restricted according to the IFRA Standards (51st Amendment). 3 perfumes also had notes of synthetic musk, a strong EDC that is prohibited under the IFRA Standards. One perfume did not mention its ingredient list at the back, a practice that is detrimental to consumer awareness and should not be happening in the first place. Conclusion/Discussion These results, supporting the initial claim, raise a dire need for the government to monitor perfume products in the market. Strict public policy is required to target the lack of awareness by mandating that the packaging clearly indicates the levels of chemicals present. Any perfume containing excessive amounts of chemicals should be restricted for manufacturing and sale.
items.authors: Mehrbano Hussain, Muhammad Hammad Khan

items.title: Excited-State Photophysics Improves Scaffold-Robust Phototoxicity Prediction and Reveals Compound-Specific State Effects
items.abstract: Phototoxicity is controlled by light absorption and access to reactive excited states, but predictive models usually encode only a single ground-state structure. Here, a physically staged representation was evaluated on 450 compounds (192 positive, 258 negative) with 10 repeated five-fold scaffold-grouped cross-validations. Structure alone gave ROC-AUC 0.745 ± 0.018 and PR-AUC 0.668 ± 0.027. Adding parent-state xTB/sTDA photophysics increased these metrics to 0.792 ± 0.012 and 0.716 ± 0.020; microstate aggregation reached 0.807 ± 0.012 and 0.726 ± 0.017, while conformer expansion plateaued at 0.808 ± 0.010 and 0.729 ± 0.017. In 10,000 paired compound bootstraps, the largest robust ranking increment was the structure-to-parent-photophysics step (ΔROC-AUC +0.0457, 95% CI +0.0274 to +0.0643). Microstates produced a smaller rank-based increment but reduced Brier error by 0.0080 (95% CI 0.0024–0.0134). Higher-level Q-Chem calculations preserved S1/T1 ordering (r = 0.946/0.931). Matched-state calculations showed large photophysical changes for avobenzone and 2-ethylanthraquinone but weak changes for pradofloxacin and ketoprofen. The results identify excited-state information as the dominant reproducible addition beyond structure and show that molecular-state effects are chemically meaningful but heterogeneous rather than universally accuracy-enhancing.
items.authors: Aris Tsai

items.title: Impact of Structural Water on Ionic Conductivity in Hydridoborates Solid Electrolytes
items.abstract: Sodium closo-hydridoborates have emerged as promising solid-state electrolytes for Na-ion batteries because of their high ionic conductivity and electrochemical stability. However, their sensitivity to water makes them challenging to scale-up. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of controlled hydration on the structure, ion transport, and interfacial stability of an anion-mixed hydridoborate, Na4(B10H10)0.5(B12H12)0.5. By exposing the hydridoborate to varying degrees of relative humidity (RH) of 30-70%, we find that hydration at 30% enables retention of its moderate Na-ion conductivity (∼0.7 mS/cm) while higher hydration levels lead to the separation of the two anions ([B10H10] 2− and [B12H12] 2−), resulting in significant disruption in the Na ion conduction pathways. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements indicate that hydration leads to the formation of distinct crystalline phases and alters the local ion coordination environments.
